mechanismOfAction:
How RABELOC RD CAPSULE Works

RABELOC RD CAPSULE works through a dual mechanism. Rabeprazole acts by reducing acid secretion at its source, ensuring a well-balanced gastric environment. Meanwhile, Domperidone restores the normal movement of the stomach and intestines, managing acid backflow and improving food passage for a more comfortable digestive experience.

Dual Mechanism Explained: Acid Control and Gut Movement

1. Acid Control through Rabeprazole:

Rabeprazole belongs to the class of proton pump modulators that reduce acid secretion at its source. Once absorbed in the intestine, it reaches the acid-producing parietal cells in the stomach lining. Here, it selectively and irreversibly binds to the H/K ATPase enzyme system, also known as the proton pump, the final step in acid secretion. By blocking the hydrogen ion exchange process, Rabeprazole manages excessive acid release into the stomach lumen, thereby increasing gastric pH. It acts faster than many other molecules in its class due to its ability to activate at higher pH levels, efficiently reducing acid production even at minimal acidity. This long-acting acid suppression helps relieve common signs of acidity and promotes a stable digestive environment.

2. Gut Movement through Domperidone:

Domperidone supports the mechanical side of digestion by enhancing gastric motility. It selectively blocks dopamine D2 receptors found in the upper gastrointestinal tract, which normally act to slow stomach contractions. By inhibiting these receptors, Domperidone increases the tone of the lower esophageal sphincter (LES), facilitates faster gastric emptying, and decreases the backward flow of food and acid into the esophagus. It also improves intestinal motion, reducing sensations of bloating, heaviness, or delayed digestion after meals, particularly useful for individuals who experience reflux linked to slow gastric transit.

3. Integrated Digestive Action:

Together, these two mechanisms form a dual-action system. Rabeprazole ensures acid stability, while Domperidone optimizes movement and clearance. This combination supports digestive comfort by minimizing acid build-up while promoting efficient passage of food through the stomach and intestines. It is particularly suited for individuals who face recurring symptoms like heartburn, acid reflux, or post-meal fullness due to poor gastric motility or high acid output. This science-backed synergy makes RABELOC RD CAPSULE effective for holistic digestive maintenance under medical supervision.

“Quick Fact Highlights” explaining why the dual combination is clinically valued
Clinically synergistic formulation: The combination of Rabeprazole (20 mg) and Domperidone (30 mg SR) works through a dual mechanism, controlling stomach acid while improving gut motility providing faster and more comprehensive relief from acid discomfort
Science-backed acid regulation: Rabeprazole acts at the final step of acid production by blocking the H/K ATPase enzyme, also known as the proton pump. This action significantly reduces acid secretion and maintains optimal pH levels in the stomach for prolonged comfort
Enhanced digestion support: Domperidone increases the movement of the stomach and upper intestinal tract, promoting quicker stomach emptying and minimizing post-meal bloating, nausea, and reflux symptoms
Faster symptom control: Rabeprazole has one of the quickest onset times among proton pump inhibitors, beginning to act within 1 hour of ingestion, offering prompt relief in cases of severe acidity and heartburn
Persistent gastric balance: The sustained-release form of Domperidone maintains smooth motility throughout the day, managing the recurrence of reflux episodes and late-night acidity, a key benefit for individuals with night-time acid reflux or delayed digestion
Improved patient quality of life: This dual approach relieves not just acid discomfort but also digestive sluggishness, making it beneficial for individuals who experience post-meal heaviness, belching, or regurgitation along with acidity
Clinically preferred for complex acid disorders: Physicians often recommend this combination when single-drug therapy (acid suppressants alone) fails to improve acid-related conditions or reflux-associated nausea
Well-tolerated and safety-monitored: The formulation has a proven safety profile when used as prescribed, with side effects such as mild headache or dizziness typically resolving with continued use
usageInstructions: For most adult users, the typical dosage is one RABELOC RD CAPSULE (Rabeprazole 20 mg + Domperidone 30 mg) taken once daily, ideally 30 minutes before a meal, preferably in the morning. The capsule must be swallowed whole with water, without crushing or chewing, to ensure proper drug release and absorption

Elderly individuals often metabolize medicines more slowly and may have pre-existing heart, kidney, or liver impairments. Therefore, they should only take the prescribed dose once daily, under close medical supervision

Long-term users may require periodic assessment of magnesium, calcium, and vitamin B12 levels, as prolonged use can mildly affect nutrient absorption. Extra caution is advised in those with osteoporosis or history of cardiac arrhythmia, as Domperidone may influence heart rhythm in predisposed individuals
usageDetails:
How to use RABELOC RD CAPSULE

Take the capsule before meals, preferably in the morning, or as directed by your healthcare provider. Swallow the capsule whole with water without crushing or chewing. Regular use under professional guidance ensures optimal results.

1. How to Take RABELOC RD CAPSULE Safely

Swallow the capsule whole with water without biting, breaking, or crushing it. The capsule should not be chewed as it is designed for delayed release. It is best taken on an empty stomach for optimal absorption and faster onset of effect. Avoid taking it with caffeinated or acidic drinks.

2. Dosage and Duration

The dosage and duration depend on your medical condition, age, and response to therapy. Most individuals experience benefits with once-daily use, but in some cases, the doctor may recommend twice-daily administration. Continue the capsule for the prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve early.

3. Dosage Guidelines for Adults and Elderly
For most adult users, the typical dosage is one RABELOC RD CAPSULE (Rabeprazole 20 mg + Domperidone 30 mg) taken once daily, ideally 30 minutes before a meal, preferably in the morning. The capsule must be swallowed whole with water, without crushing or chewing, to ensure proper drug release and absorption
Elderly individuals often metabolize medicines more slowly and may have pre-existing heart, kidney, or liver impairments. Therefore, they should only take the prescribed dose once daily, under close medical supervision
Long-term users may require periodic assessment of magnesium, calcium, and vitamin B12 levels, as prolonged use can mildly affect nutrient absorption. Extra caution is advised in those with osteoporosis or history of cardiac arrhythmia, as Domperidone may influence heart rhythm in predisposed individuals

More Information
Why RABELOC RD CAPSULE is Doctor-Recommended for “Digestive Balance.”

Digestive discomfort caused by acidity and reflux is often linked to two simultaneous problems excess acid formation and slowed stomach movement.RABELOC RD CAPSULE addresses both through a clinically trusted dual mechanism combining Rabeprazole and Domperidone. Doctors recommend this capsule because it supports digestive balance by managing acid levels and enhancing gastric motility, offering smoother stomach function throughout the day.

“Did You Know?” Sidebar: Use small fact highlights like: “Over 70% of acidity cases are linked to late-night meals. Following early dinner routines may reduce reflux frequency”
Over 70% of acidity cases are linked to nighttime eating habits, eating late dinners or snacks within two hours of bedtime significantly increases reflux risk. Having meals earlier in the evening can reduce acid backflow and discomfort.
Meal timing matters: Studies show that eating dinner 3–4 hours before sleep supports better digestion and reduces nighttime acid episodes. Early dining allows the stomach to empty properly before lying down.
Late-night meals affect sleep and metabolism: Research indicates that those who regularly eat after 9 p.m. experience disrupted sleep patterns, slower calorie burning, and more frequent heartburn sensations compared to early eaters.
Fast eating can upset digestive balance: People who eat quickly swallow more air, which increases pressure in the stomach and raises the chance of acid discomfort. Chewing food slowly and mindfully can reduce symptoms and aid smoother digestion.
Simple posture shifts help: Standing or staying upright after meals even for 15–20 minutes can minimize reflux frequency and relieve heaviness. Avoid lying flat immediately after eating.
Diet quality counts: Frequent consumption of spicy, oily, or fried foods can raise stomach acid levels. Choosing gentle foods like oatmeal, bananas, and green vegetables can maintain a neutral digestive pH.
Hydration supports healthy acid balance: Drinking plain water throughout the day dilutes acid concentration naturally. However, sipping slowly instead of gulping helps avoid trapped air and bloating.

introduction:
Introduction About RENVORAB SL CAPSULE

RENVORAB SL CAPSULE is a combination of Levosulpiride and Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Dopamine D2 antagonists and Proton-pump inhibitors respectively. RENVORAB SL CAPSULE is indicated for the management of Gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD). GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the esophagus leading to irritation and inflammation of lining of food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

RENVORAB SL CAPSULE can also be used to manage peptic ulcer (painful sores in the gut), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid), functional dyspepsia (recurrent signs and symptoms of indigestion without an obvious cause) and diabetic gastroparesis (delayed gastric emptying caused due to diabetes).

Take RENVORAB SL CAPSULE preferably on an empty stomach. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking RENVORAB SL CAPSULE as it could potentiate the CNS depressive side effects.

Patients receiving long-term management (>1 year) with RENVORAB SL CAPSULE should be kept on regular surveillance because it can increase the risk of bone fracture (i.e., in the hip, wrist or spine) which is more predominant in the patients having osteoporosis or taking corticosteroids.

Before taking RENVORAB SL CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you have any heart, kidney or liver disease as a precaution. RENVORAB SL CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant or breastfeeding women, including children and adolescents (aged below 18 years).

The most common side effects of taking RENVORAB SL CAPSULE are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation and headache. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsen.

introduction:
Introduction About ZUROPRAZ 20MG TABLET

ZUROPRAZ 20MG TABLET contains Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Proton pump inhibitors. It is used to manage Gastro-esophageal Reflux Disease (GERD), peptic ulcer and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumours in the pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid).

GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the oesophagus leading to the irritation of lining of the food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

Peptic ulcers are painful sores that develop on the linings of the stomach, oesophagus and/or intestines. Symptoms include stomach pain, flatulence, indigestion, vomiting and fatigue.

Take ZUROPRAZ 20MG TABLET preferably before meals or as directed by the physician. Before taking ZUROPRAZ 20MG TABLET inform your doctor if you have any liver problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have vitamin B12 deficiency, osteoporosis or any tumors in your stomach.

Do not take ZUROPRAZ 20MG TABLET if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without consulting your doctor. The most common side effects of taking ZUROPRAZ 20MG TABLET are oral sores, constipation, indigestion, stomach pain, headache and dizziness. Consult your doctor if any of the side effect troubles you.

You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience severe uncontrollable diarrhea with stomach pain or tenderness after taking ZUROPRAZ 20MG TABLET.

mechanismOfAction:
How ZUROPRAZ 20MG TABLET Works

ZUROPRAZ 20MG TABLET is a proton pump inhibitor. It reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach by blocking the actions of an enzyme called H+ K+ ATPase (also known as proton pump) which is present in the lining of the stomach walls. As a result, it reduces the chances for acid reflux into the oesophagus, heals peptic ulcers and esophageal lesions and manages its recurrence.

How to use ZUROPRAZ 20MG TABLET

Take ZUROPRAZ 20MG TABLET as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. It is preferably taken in the mornings or at any time of the day before meals.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About PANZEC 40MG TABLET

PANZEC 40MG TABLET contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking PANZEC 40MG TABLET as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking PANZEC 40MG TABLET, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How PANZEC 40MG TABLET Works

PANZEC 40MG TABLET contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why PANZEC 40MG TABLET Is Effective for Acid Control:
PANZEC 40MG TABLET effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take PANZEC 40MG TABLET?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

introduction:
Introduction About PEPTARD 20MG TABLET

PEPTARD 20MG TABLET contains Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Proton pump inhibitors. It is used to manage Gastro-esophageal Reflux Disease (GERD), peptic ulcer and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumours in the pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid).

GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the oesophagus leading to the irritation of lining of the food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

Peptic ulcers are painful sores that develop on the linings of the stomach, oesophagus and/or intestines. Symptoms include stomach pain, flatulence, indigestion, vomiting and fatigue.

Take PEPTARD 20MG TABLET preferably before meals or as directed by the physician. Before taking PEPTARD 20MG TABLET inform your doctor if you have any liver problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have vitamin B12 deficiency, osteoporosis or any tumors in your stomach.

Do not take PEPTARD 20MG TABLET if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without consulting your doctor. The most common side effects of taking PEPTARD 20MG TABLET are oral sores, constipation, indigestion, stomach pain, headache and dizziness. Consult your doctor if any of the side effect troubles you.

You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience severe uncontrollable diarrhea with stomach pain or tenderness after taking PEPTARD 20MG TABLET.

PEPTARD 20MG TABLET is a proton pump inhibitor. It reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach by blocking the actions of an enzyme called H+ K+ ATPase (also known as proton pump) which is present in the lining of the stomach walls. introduction:
Introduction About PANCICARE TABLET

PANCICARE TABLET contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking PANCICARE TABLET as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking PANCICARE TABLET, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How PANCICARE TABLET Works

PANCICARE TABLET contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why PANCICARE TABLET Is Effective for Acid Control:
PANCICARE TABLET effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take PANCICARE TABLET?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

Introduction About PANPOT DSR CAPSULE

PANPOT DSR CAPSULE is used to manage peptic ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reflux esophagitis. It is a combination of Domperidone and Pantoprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic Drugs and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. PANPOT DSR CAPSULE acts by reducing the production of gastric acid. It also speeds up the movement of food from the stomach to the intestines, thereby reducing the signs of nausea, vomiting and acid reflux. Due to these actions, it can also reduce the unpleasant signs of GI tract such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion, burping, bloating, acidity or heartburn.

It should be taken at least 15-30 minutes before meals. During management with PANPOT DSR CAPSULE your doctor will closely monitor your kidney functions, liver functions and blood magnesium levels to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects. Before taking PANPOT DSR CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any blockage or tears in the gut or have weak bones.

PANPOT DSR CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients bleeding from the gut. Consult your doctor before taking PANPOT DSR CAPSULE if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. The most common side effects are dryness of mouth, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect bothers you. You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience any signs of low magnesium levels in blood (such as tiredness, abnormal muscle movements, dizziness, confusion, disorientation, irregular heartbeat).

mechanismOfAction:
How PANPOT DSR CAPSULE Works

PANPOT DSR CAPSULE contains Domperidone and Pantoprazole. Domperidone is a prokinetic medicine with anti-emetic properties which works by blocking the actions of a chemical messenger called dopamine in the gut and across the brain and spinal cord. This action stimulates the gut, reduces acid reflux and speeds up the movements of food from the stomach into the intestines. It also blocks the transmission of nerve signals between the vomiting centers and brain which reduces the onset of nausea and vomiting. Pantoprazole reduces gastric acid secretion by the blocking the actions of a protein membrane called H+K+Atpase (proton pump) present in the lining of the stomach. By reducing stomach acid production, PANPOT DSR CAPSULE it manages the worsening of ulcers, heals the existing ulcers and esophageal lesions and provides relief from the unpleasant symptoms of GI tract (such as acidity, bloating, burping and indigestion).

introduction:
Introduction About PANSEC 40MG INJECTION

PANSEC 40MG INJECTION contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking PANSEC 40MG INJECTION as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking PANSEC 40MG INJECTION, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How PANSEC 40MG INJECTION Works

PANSEC 40MG INJECTION contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why PANSEC 40MG INJECTION Is Effective for Acid Control:
PANSEC 40MG INJECTION effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take PANSEC 40MG INJECTION?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

introduction:
Introduction About MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL)

MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL) is used to manage gastrointestinal disorders manifested with hyperacidity and increased gas production. It may be administered as monotherapy or to manage gastro-oesophagitis reflux, chronic diarrhea, and non-ulcer dyspepsia. MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL) contains Aluminium hydroxide, Magnesium hydroxide, and oxetacaine, which belong to a group of medicines called Antacids and Local anaesthetics, respectively.

MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL) is not recommended for patients with chronic renal failure. Patients should be advised not to take any oral medication within 1 to 2 hours of taking MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL), as it has potential interactions with other medicines. Patients should be informed that MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL) held for a long time in the mouth may impair taste sensation because of its oxetacaine content.

Patients should be advised not to exceed the prescribed amounts of MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL), as it may cause hypersensitive reactions. mechanismOfAction:
How MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL) Works

MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL) is a combination of Aluminium hydroxide, Magnesium hydroxide, and Oxetacaine. Aluminium hydroxide acts on the hydrochloric acid in the stomach by neutralizing it, forming Aluminium chloride salt and water. Magnesium hydroxide increases peristaltic activity, causing osmotic retention of fluids, thus resulting in bowel evacuation. It also reduces stomach acid by reacting with hydrochloric acid to form magnesium chloride. Oxetacaine is a topical anaesthetic that effectively relieves pain when applied to the mouth and food pipelining. The antacids neutralize stomach acid and reduce further irritation of the food pipe. Antacid also thickens the liquid to help carry the oxetacaine and coat the food pipe.
usageDetails:
How to use MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL)

Take MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL) as advised by your physician. Shake well before use. Take MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL) 1 to 2 teaspoonfuls 4 times a day, 15 minutes before each meal and at bedtime. It is preferable to take MUCAINE ORANGE GEL(ORAL) undiluted. However, a sip of water may be taken if desired. The correct dose and duration for you will be decided by the doctor depending upon your age, body weight, and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About REBAGEN OTIC CAPSULE

REBAGEN OTIC CAPSULE is a combination of N-Acetylcysteine, Alpha lipoic acid, and Rebamipide which belongs to the group of medicines called Mucolytic agent, Antioxidants and Mucolytic agent respectively. It is used to manage hearing loss especially in old age.

Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking this medicine. REBAGEN OTIC CAPSULE is not recommended in patients with asthma. REBAGEN OTIC CAPSULE should be used with caution in patients with liver and kidney disease, high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, stomach ulcer, bleeding problems, undergoing any surgeries, diabetes, thyroid problems, anaemia, cancer, or vitamin-B1 (thiamine deficiency).

REBAGEN OTIC CAPSULE should be used with caution in pregnant and breastfeeding women. REBAGEN OTIC CAPSULE should be used with caution with elderly patients. The most common side effects of taking REBAGEN OTIC CAPSULE are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, constipation, diarrhoea, and skin rash. Contact your doctor if any of the symptoms get worse.
uses: It is used to manage hearing loss
usesDetails:
Uses Of REBAGEN OTIC CAPSULE
It is used to manage hearing loss
mechanismOfAction:
How REBAGEN OTIC CAPSULE Works

REBAGEN OTIC CAPSULE is an antioxidant combination that works by reducing ear damage and promoting ear cell preservation. N-Acetylcysteine and alpha lipoic acid works by increasing glutathione levels (antioxidant), and other free radical-producing substances that detoxify the body, reduce the inflammatory response, increase metabolism of mitochondrial energy, and significantly protect cells. Rebamipide is an mucoprotective agent which increases the soluble mucus, mucosal blood flow, and inhibits the production of inflammatory cytokines.

Take REBAGEN OTIC CAPSULE as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Depending on your age, body weight, disease condition, your doctor will fix the correct dose and duration for you.

introduction:
Introduction About AUXISODA EC 1000 TABLET

AUXISODA EC 1000 Tablet is an alkalinizing agent used to correct metabolic acidosis (increased acidity of blood and urine). It can also be used as a replacement therapy for patients suffering from severe diarrhea and can manage injection site irritation in patients receiving IV fluids or injections.

It contains sodium bicarbonate as the active ingredient which is a base (alkaline) compound. Following consumption, sodium bicarbonate restores the pH of blood and urine to the normal levels and reverses the clinical manifestations of metabolic acidosis.

Use AUXISODA EC 1000 Tablet only as advised by your doctor. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Do not exceed the daily recommended dosage.

Before taking AUXISODA EC 1000 Tablet, inform your doctor if you have breathing problems, heart problems, kidney problems, liver problems, high blood pressure, high blood sodium levels or swollen foot or ankles. You must also inform your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding as a precaution.

Do not take AUXISODA EC 1000 Tablet if you have metabolic alkalosis (increased pH of blood and urine), excessive vomiting or hypocalcemia (low blood calcium levels) or if you are undergoing continuous gastrointestinal suction.

The most common side effects of taking this medicine are nausea, vomiting, headache, muscle pain, constipation, dry mouth, increased thirst, skin ulcerations, tiredness and edema. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect troubles you.

introduction:
Introduction About ACTAPRO 100MG TABLET

ACTAPRO 100MG TABLET contains Acotiamide, which belongs to the group of medicines called Gastro-intestinal agents. It is used in the management of functional dyspepsia. Functional dyspepsia is a chronic functional disorder of the upper digestive system that affects sensation and movement.

The symptoms of functional dyspepsia in affected individuals include a burning sensation in the stomach, bloating, burping, nausea (after meals), an early feeling of fullness (satiety), and stomach pain. Your doctor may advise you to take relevant tests to evaluate and understand your existing condition.

ACTAPRO 100MG TABLET is not recommended for use in patients who are allergic to acotiamide. Before taking ACTAPRO 100MG TABLET, inform your doctor if you have liver problems (such as hepatic impairment) and/or kidney problems (such as renal impairment). The most common side effects of taking ACTAPRO 100MG TABLET are diarrhoea, constipation, nausea, vomiting, rash, and/or red itchy welts. Consult your doctor if any of your symptoms get worse or persist.
usesDetails:
Uses Of ACTAPRO 100MG TABLET
Manage functional dyspepsia
mechanismOfAction:
How ACTAPRO 100MG TABLET Works

ACTAPRO 100MG TABLET works by increasing acetylcholine concentration in the stomach, which helps to promote the movement of foods from the stomach into the intestine and also increases intestinal motility. As a result, it helps to manage and relieve the functional disorders of the upper digestive system.
usageDetails:

Take ACTAPRO 100MG TABLET as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of the management for you depending on your age, body weight, and disease condition.

Introduction About XYLOPAN 40 TABLET

XYLOPAN 40 TABLET contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking XYLOPAN 40 TABLET as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking XYLOPAN 40 TABLET, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How XYLOPAN 40 TABLET Works

XYLOPAN 40 TABLET contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why XYLOPAN 40 TABLET Is Effective for Acid Control:
XYLOPAN 40 TABLET effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take XYLOPAN 40 TABLET?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
Long-term use may increase the risk of side effects such as bone fractures or low magnesium levels; regular monitoring may be required.
Report any unusual symptoms, such as persistent diarrhea, muscle cramps, or rash, to your doctor promptly.

Do not stop taking the medicine suddenly without consulting your doctor, even if your symptoms improve.
usageDetails:
How to use XYLOPAN 40 TABLET
How to Take XYLOPAN 40 TABLET:

Follow your doctor's instructions regarding the exact dosage. Do not exceed the recommended daily dosage.XYLOPAN 40 TABLET should be swallowed whole with a glass of water. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet, as this may affect its effectiveness. Take the medicine exactly as prescribed by your doctor for the best results.

XYLOPAN 40 TABLET Dosage Instructions:

The dosage of XYLOPAN 40 TABLET depends on your medical condition and response to management. It is usually taken once daily, but your doctor may adjust the dose based on the severity of your symptoms or the specific condition being treated. Always follow your doctor’s instructions regarding the dose and duration of management.

When Should You Take XYLOPAN 40 TABLET?

XYLOPAN 40 TABLET is best taken at least 1 hour before a meal, preferably in the morning. Taking it on an empty stomach allows for better absorption and maximum effectiveness.

Precautions While Taking XYLOPAN 40 TABLET:
Inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking HIV medications, have a history of allergic reactions to similar medicines, or suffer from osteoporosis.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
Long-term use may increase the risk of side effects such as bone fractures or low magnesium levels; regular monitoring may be required.
Report any unusual symptoms, such as persistent diarrhea, muscle cramps, or rash, to your doctor promptly.
Tips for Best Results with XYLOPAN 40 TABLET:
Take the tablet at the same time each day to maintain consistent levels in your body.
Avoid caffeinated drinks (such as tea and coffee), spicy or fatty foods, and large meals, as these can worsen acidity.
Eat smaller, more frequent meals instead of large ones.
Do not stop taking the medicine suddenly without consulting your doctor, even if your symptoms improve.

sideEffectsDetails:
Side Effects Of XYLOPAN 40 TABLET

Like all medicines, XYLOPAN 40 TABLET may cause certain side effects in some individuals, although not everybody gets them.

The most common side effects of taking XYLOPAN 40 TABLET are:
Nausea
Vomiting
Headache
Dizziness
Flatulence
Diarrhea
Stomach pain
Constipation
Rash
When to consult your doctor?
Severe allergic reactions symptoms such as rash, itching or swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing
Irregular heartbeat or palpitations
Severe or persistent diarrhea
Low magnesium levels symptoms such as seizures or muscle spasms
Severe unusual tiredness or weakness
Kidney problems symptoms such as changes in the amount of urine, blood in urine, or swelling of the legs
Lupus symptoms such as joint pain or a rash on the cheeks or arms

warnings.details: Consult your doctor before taking XYLOPAN 40 TABLET if you are pregnant, as its safety during pregnancy has not been well established. Consult your doctor before taking this medicine.
XYLOPAN 40 TABLET should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. Inform your doctor if you are breastfeeding before taking this medicine.
XYLOPAN 40 TABLET is unlikely to affect your ability to drive or operate machinery. However, if you experience dizziness or visual disturbances, avoid such activities until you feel well.
Avoid consuming alcohol while taking XYLOPAN 40 TABLET, as it may worsen your symptoms or increase the risk of side effects.
XYLOPAN 40 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Dose adjustments or monitoring may be required. Consult your doctor before taking this medicine.
XYLOPAN 40 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with liver problems. Consult your doctor before taking this medicine.
Do not take XYLOPAN 40 TABLET if you are allergic to pantoprazole or any other ingredients of this medicine. Inform your doctor about any previous allergic reactions to similar medicines.
XYLOPAN 40 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with heart problems. Consult your doctor before taking this medicine.
XYLOPAN 40 TABLET is not recommended for use in children below 12 years of age, as its safety and efficacy have not been established in this age group. Consult your pediatrician before giving it.
XYLOPAN 40 TABLET should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years and above). Dose adjustments and regular monitoring may be necessary. Consult your doctor before taking it.

More Information
01.What makes XYLOPAN 40 TABLET a preferred choice over other medications?
Potent and Long-Lasting Acid Suppression: XYLOPAN 40 TABLET contains pantoprazole, a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that effectively blocks the final step of stomach acid production, providing stronger and longer-lasting relief from symptoms like heartburn, acid reflux, and indigestion compared to H2 blockers or antacids.
Comprehensive Symptom Relief and Healing: It not only relieves discomfort from acid-related conditions but also promotes healing of stomach and duodenal ulcers, and helps manage more severe conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
Lowering with Painkiller Use: XYLOPAN 40 TABLET is recommended for lowering stomach ulcers and acidity in patients who require long-term use of painkillers (NSAIDs), a benefit not offered by all acid-reducing medicines.
Convenient Once-Daily Dosing: Its long duration of action allows for once-daily dosing, making it easier for patients to adhere to treatment and maintain consistent acid control.
Favorable Tolerability Profile: Most side effects are mild and temporary, such as headache, nausea, or diarrhea. Serious side effects are rare when used as directed, and the risk of complications can be minimized with appropriate monitoring.
Well-Studied and Trusted: Pantoprazole, the active ingredient, is widely used and supported by extensive clinical experience, ensuring both efficacy and safety for a broad range of patients.

These advantages make XYLOPAN 40 TABLET a reliable and effective option for both short-term relief and long-term management of acid-related disorders, often outperforming less potent or shorter-acting alternatives.

introduction:
Introduction About RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID

RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID is a combination of Aluminium Hydroxide, Magnesium Hydroxide, and Sodium Alginate which belongs to the group of medicines called Antacids, Laxatives, and Polysaccharides respectively. It is used to relieve the discomfort of indigestion and heartburn including heartburn in pregnancy, reflux oesophagitis, gastric reflux, and acid indigestion.

RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID is not recommended to use in patients having peptic ulcers. Before taking RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID inform your doctor if you have kidney problems or are on a low-phosphorous diet. Caution must be exercised while giving RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID to pregnant and breastfeeding women.

RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID is not recommended to use in children under 6 years of age and it should be used with caution in children 6 years of age and above and elderly patients. The most common side effects of using RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID are flatulence (wind). Ask for your doctor’s advice if any of these worsen or don’t improve.
usesDetails:
Uses Of RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID

It is used to relieve the discomfort of indigestion and heartburn including;

Heartburn in pregnancy
Reflux oesophagitis
Gastric reflux
Acid indigestion
mechanismOfAction:
How RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID Works

RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID helps in the management of various gastrointestinal problems Aluminium Hydroxide is an Antacid that acts by neutralizing the hydrochloric acid produced by the stomach. It also decreases the pH level in the stomach, stabilizing acidity. Magnesium hydroxide is a Laxative that works by drawing in more water in the intestinal tract. This increases intestinal movements and helps in easy bowel emptying. Sodium alginate reacts with the acid in the stomach to form a thick gel-like layer. These gum-like substances (insoluble compounds) float on the gastric fluids to protect the esophagus from acid exposure and provide relief from the symptoms.
usageDetails:
How to use RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID

Take RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID as advised by your physician. Shake well before use. Take RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID preferably 15 minutes before meals. It is preferable to take it without diluting it. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you depending on your age, disease condition, and body weight.

Common
Flatulence
Rare

Stop taking RIFLUX FORTE LIQUID and contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects:

Heartburn or stomach pain continues

More Information
01.What makes PROTERA 40MG INJECTION a preferred choice over other medications?
Potent and Long-Lasting Acid Suppression: PROTERA 40MG INJECTION contains pantoprazole, a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that effectively blocks the final step of stomach acid production, providing stronger and longer-lasting relief from symptoms like heartburn, acid reflux, and indigestion compared to H2 blockers or antacids.
Comprehensive Symptom Relief and Healing: It not only relieves discomfort from acid-related conditions but also promotes healing of stomach and duodenal ulcers, and helps manage more severe conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
Lowering with Painkiller Use: PROTERA 40MG INJECTION is recommended for lowering stomach ulcers and acidity in patients who require long-term use of painkillers (NSAIDs), a benefit not offered by all acid-reducing medicines.
Convenient Once-Daily Dosing: Its long duration of action allows for once-daily dosing, making it easier for patients to adhere to treatment and maintain consistent acid control.
Favorable Tolerability Profile: Most side effects are mild and temporary, such as headache, nausea, or diarrhea. Serious side effects are rare when used as directed, and the risk of complications can be minimized with appropriate monitoring.
Well-Studied and Trusted: Pantoprazole, the active ingredient, is widely used and supported by extensive clinical experience, ensuring both efficacy and safety for a broad range of patients.

These advantages make PROTERA 40MG INJECTION a reliable and effective option for both short-term relief and long-term management of acid-related disorders, often outperforming less potent or shorter-acting alternatives.

introduction:
Introduction About NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE

NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE is used to manage peptic ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reflux esophagitis. It is a combination of Domperidone and Pantoprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic Drugs and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE acts by reducing the production of gastric acid. It also speeds up the movement of food from the stomach to the intestines, thereby reducing the signs of nausea, vomiting and acid reflux. Due to these actions, it can also reduce the unpleasant signs of GI tract such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion, burping, bloating, acidity or heartburn.

It should be taken at least 15-30 minutes before meals. During management with NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE your doctor will closely monitor your kidney functions, liver functions and blood magnesium levels to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects. Before taking NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any blockage or tears in the gut or have weak bones.

NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients bleeding from the gut. Consult your doctor before taking NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. The most common side effects are dryness of mouth, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect bothers you. You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience any signs of low magnesium levels in blood (such as tiredness, abnormal muscle movements, dizziness, confusion, disorientation, irregular heartbeat).

mechanismOfAction:
How NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE Works

NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE contains Domperidone and Pantoprazole. Domperidone is a prokinetic medicine with anti-emetic properties which works by blocking the actions of a chemical messenger called dopamine in the gut and across the brain and spinal cord. This action stimulates the gut, reduces acid reflux and speeds up the movements of food from the stomach into the intestines. It also blocks the transmission of nerve signals between the vomiting centers and brain which reduces the onset of nausea and vomiting. Pantoprazole reduces gastric acid secretion by the blocking the actions of a protein membrane called H+K+Atpase (proton pump) present in the lining of the stomach. By reducing stomach acid production, NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE it manages the worsening of ulcers, heals the existing ulcers and esophageal lesions and provides relief from the unpleasant symptoms of GI tract (such as acidity, bloating, burping and indigestion).

NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients with heart problems such as prolongation of QT interval or congestive heart failure.

Others

NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you:

Have bloody stools or bleeding in the gut
Have blockage or tear in the intestines
Have severe fluid or electrolyte disturbances
Have prolactinoma (a non-cancerous tumor of pituitary gland)
Have low blood potassium or magnesium levels

Before taking NUPENTA DSR CAPSULE inform your doctor if you:

Have osteoporosis
Have vitamin B12 deficiency (sore tongue, mouth ulcers, pale skin, depression)
Are going to test Chromogranin A level

introduction:
Introduction About PANTOMAC INJECTION

PANTOMAC INJECTION contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking PANTOMAC INJECTION as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking PANTOMAC INJECTION, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How PANTOMAC INJECTION Works

PANTOMAC INJECTION contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why PANTOMAC INJECTION Is Effective for Acid Control:
PANTOMAC INJECTION effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take PANTOMAC INJECTION?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

introduction:
Introduction About PANMINT 40 TABLET

PANMINT 40 TABLET contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking PANMINT 40 TABLET as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking PANMINT 40 TABLET, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How PANMINT 40 TABLET Works

PANMINT 40 TABLET contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why PANMINT 40 TABLET Is Effective for Acid Control:
PANMINT 40 TABLET effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take PANMINT 40 TABLET?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

introduction:
Introduction About OCID DSR CAPSULE

OCID DSR CAPSULE is a combination of Domperidone and Omeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic Drugs and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. It is used to manage peptic ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumours in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid).

OCID DSR CAPSULE is effective in managing peptic ulcer caused either due to stomach infection (H. pylori infection) or due to prolong use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (such as ibuprofen, aceclofenac). OCID DSR CAPSULEacts by reducing the production of gastric acid. It also speeds up the movement of food from the stomach to the intestines, thereby reducing the signs of nausea, vomiting and acid reflux. Due to these actions, it can also reduce the unpleasant signs of GI tract such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion, burping, bloating, acidity or heartburn. OCID DSR CAPSULEis suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 12 years or above weighing 35 kg or more). It should be taken at least 15-30 minutes before meals. During management with OCID DSR CAPSULEyour doctor will closely monitor your kidney functions, liver functions and blood magnesium levels to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before taking OCID DSR CAPSULEinform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any blockage or tears in the gut or have weak bones. OCID DSR CAPSULEis not recommended for use in patients having bleeding from the gut. Consult your doctor before taking OCID DSR CAPSULEif you are pregnant or breastfeeding. The most common side effects of taking OCID DSR CAPSULEare dryness of mouth, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect bothers you. You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience any abnormal signs such as unusual tiredness, abnormal muscle movements, dizziness, confusion, disorientation, irregular heartbeat, fragile bones, bloody stools or vomits or sudden weight loss.

mechanismOfAction:
How OCID DSR CAPSULE Works

OCID DSR CAPSULE contains two medicines namely domperidone and omeprazole. Domperidone works by blocking the actions of a chemical messenger called dopamine in the gut and across the brain and spinal cord. This action stimulates the gut, reduces acid reflux and speeds up the movements of food from the stomach into the intestines. It also blocks the transmission of nerve signals between the vomiting centres and the brain which reduces the onset of nausea and vomiting. Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor. It reduces gastric acid secretion by the blocking the actions of a protein membrane called H+K+Atpase (proton pump) present in the lining of the stomach. By reducing stomach acid production, OCID DSR CAPSULEmanages the worsening of ulcers, heals the existing ulcers and esophageal lesions and provides relief from the unpleasant symptoms of GI tract (such as acidity, bloating, burping and indigestion).

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition. Do not stop taking OCID DSR CAPSULEunless your doctor advice you to stop.

introduction:
Introduction About PENDOM OD CAPSULE

PENDOM OD CAPSULE is used to manage peptic ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reflux esophagitis. It is a combination of Domperidone and Pantoprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic Drugs and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. PENDOM OD CAPSULE acts by reducing the production of gastric acid. It also speeds up the movement of food from the stomach to the intestines, thereby reducing the signs of nausea, vomiting and acid reflux. Due to these actions, it can also reduce the unpleasant signs of GI tract such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion, burping, bloating, acidity or heartburn.

It should be taken at least 15-30 minutes before meals. During management with PENDOM OD CAPSULE your doctor will closely monitor your kidney functions, liver functions and blood magnesium levels to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects. Before taking PENDOM OD CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any blockage or tears in the gut or have weak bones.

PENDOM OD CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients bleeding from the gut. Consult your doctor before taking PENDOM OD CAPSULE if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. The most common side effects are dryness of mouth, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect bothers you. You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience any signs of low magnesium levels in blood (such as tiredness, abnormal muscle movements, dizziness, confusion, disorientation, irregular heartbeat).

mechanismOfAction:
How PENDOM OD CAPSULE Works

PENDOM OD CAPSULE contains Domperidone and Pantoprazole. Domperidone is a prokinetic medicine with anti-emetic properties which works by blocking the actions of a chemical messenger called dopamine in the gut and across the brain and spinal cord. This action stimulates the gut, reduces acid reflux and speeds up the movements of food from the stomach into the intestines. It also blocks the transmission of nerve signals between the vomiting centers and brain which reduces the onset of nausea and vomiting. Pantoprazole reduces gastric acid secretion by the blocking the actions of a protein membrane called H+K+Atpase (proton pump) present in the lining of the stomach. By reducing stomach acid production, PENDOM OD CAPSULE it manages the worsening of ulcers, heals the existing ulcers and esophageal lesions and provides relief from the unpleasant symptoms of GI tract (such as acidity, bloating, burping and indigestion).

PENDOM OD CAPSULE may pass through breast milk. Therefore, it should be used in breastfeeding women only if it is considered necessary by the physician.
PENDOM OD CAPSULE does not affect your ability in driving or handling heavy tools or machines. However, do not drive or handle heavy tools or machines if your ability is affected by the medicine.
Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking PENDOM OD CAPSULE, as it could aggravate your existing condition.
PENDOM OD CAPSULE should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems.

Do not take PENDOM OD CAPSULE if you are allergic to Domperidone, Pantoprazole or to any other ingredients of this medicine.
PENDOM OD CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients with heart problems such as prolongation of QT interval or congestive heart failure.
PENDOM OD CAPSULE is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years).
PENDOM OD CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years and above).

Others

PENDOM OD CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you:

Have bloody stools or bleeding in the gut
Have blockage or tear in the intestines
Have severe fluid or electrolyte disturbances
Have prolactinoma (a non-cancerous tumor of pituitary gland)
Have low blood potassium or magnesium levels

Before taking PENDOM OD CAPSULE inform your doctor if you:

Have osteoporosis
Have vitamin B12 deficiency (sore tongue, mouth ulcers, pale skin, depression)
Are going to test Chromogranin A level

name: OMIMAC 20 Capsule 20's
introduction:
Introduction About OMIMAC 20 CAPSULE

OMIMAC 20 CAPSULE is used in the management of gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (acid contents in the stomach flows back into the tube connecting the mouth and stomach causing heartburn, nausea, vomiting, bitter taste, discomfort in upper abdomen) in children (above 1 years of age) and adults. It is used in adults to manage gastric (stomach), duodenal ulcer (upper part of the intestine), ulcers infected with Helicobacter pylori bacteria in addition with antibiotics (including children) and ulcers due to the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Also, it is used in adults to manage Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It contains Omeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Proton pump inhibitors that effectively lowers the amount of acid produced in the stomach by irreversibly binding to and inhibiting the hydrogen-potassium ATPase pump that resides on the lining of the digestive tract. This kind of action helps to reduce vomiting, promote healing of damaged stomach tissue in ulcers.

OMIMAC 20 CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients with history of allergic reactions to omeprazole or any other proton pump inhibitors (Ex. pantoprazole, lansoprazole, rabeprazole and esomeprazole). Before taking OMIMAC 20 CAPSULE, tell your doctor if you have any severe liver problems, weight loss, swallowing problems, stomach pain or indigestion, osteoporosis (condition in which bones become weak and brittle), vitamin B12 deficiency, schedule for specific blood test (chromogranin A).

OMIMAC 20 CAPSULE can be used in pregnant and breast-feeding women only if advised by the doctor. OMIMAC 20 CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged above 65 years) due to increased risk of fractures. The most common side effects of taking OMIMAC 20 CAPSULE are headache, diarrhoea, stomach pain, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects bothers you.
