name: SUCRACHEM Suspension 100ml
introduction:
Introduction About SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION

SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION contains Sucralfate, which belongs to the group of medicines called Anti-ulcer agents. It is used for the short-term (up to 8 weeks) management of active duodenal ulcers (part of the small intestine), prophylaxis of gastrointestinal haemorrhage due to stress ulceration in critically ill patients, gastric and benign ulcers.

SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION should be used with caution in patients with chronic renal failure, dialysis patients and diabetes. SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION should be used with caution in pregnant and breastfeeding women. The safety and effectiveness of SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION for use in children have not been established.

SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION should be used with caution in elderly patients above 65 years of age. The most common side effect of taking SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION is constipation. Consult your doctor if any of your symptoms get worse or persist.
uses: Management of active duodenal ulcer, benign and gastric ulcers
usesDetails:
Uses Of SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION
Management of active duodenal ulcer, benign and gastric ulcers
Prophylaxis management of gastrointestinal haemorrhage
mechanismOfAction:
How SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION Works

SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION works by forming a protective layer around the ulcer saving it from the further attack of acid, pepsin or bile. It increases growth factor production, promoting tissue growth, regeneration, thereby facilitating repair.
usageDetails:
How to use SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION

Take SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION as advised by your physician. Shake well before each use. Take SUCRACHEM SUSPENSIONon an empty stomach at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal for best results. Your doctor will determine the correct dose and duration for you based on your age, body weight and disease condition.

SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION should be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it is not known whether it passes into breast milk. Contact your doctor before taking SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION.
Do not drive or operate any machines if you feel any unusual effects after taking SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION.
SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION should be used with caution in patients with chronic kidney failure and patients undergoing dialysis. Contact your doctor before taking SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION.

SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION should be used with caution in elderly patients aged 65 years or above, especially with decreased liver, kidney and cardiac function or other diseases. Contact your doctor before taking SUCRACHEM SUSPENSION.

name: Rabifast 20mg Tablet 15'S
introduction:
Introduction About RABIFAST 20MG TABLET

RABIFAST 20MG TABLET contains Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Proton pump inhibitors. It is used to manage Gastro-esophageal Reflux Disease (GERD), peptic ulcer and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumours in the pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid).

GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the oesophagus leading to the irritation of lining of the food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

Peptic ulcers are painful sores that develop on the linings of the stomach, oesophagus and/or intestines. Symptoms include stomach pain, flatulence, indigestion, vomiting and fatigue.

Take RABIFAST 20MG TABLET preferably before meals or as directed by the physician. Before taking RABIFAST 20MG TABLET inform your doctor if you have any liver problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have vitamin B12 deficiency, osteoporosis or any tumors in your stomach.

Do not take RABIFAST 20MG TABLET if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without consulting your doctor. The most common side effects of taking RABIFAST 20MG TABLET are oral sores, constipation, indigestion, stomach pain, headache and dizziness. Consult your doctor if any of the side effect troubles you.

You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience severe uncontrollable diarrhea with stomach pain or tenderness after taking RABIFAST 20MG TABLET.
usesDetails:
Uses Of RABIFAST 20MG TABLET
Manage Gastro-Esophageal Reflux Disease
Manage and Manages Peptic ulcers
Manage Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
mechanismOfAction:
How RABIFAST 20MG TABLET Works

RABIFAST 20MG TABLET is a proton pump inhibitor. It reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach by blocking the actions of an enzyme called H+ K+ ATPase (also known as proton pump) which is present in the lining of the stomach walls. As a result, it reduces the chances for acid reflux into the oesophagus, heals peptic ulcers and esophageal lesions and manages its recurrence.
usageDetails:
How to use RABIFAST 20MG TABLET

Take RABIFAST 20MG TABLET as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. It is preferably taken in the mornings or at any time of the day before meals.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About OMECER 10MG CAPSULE

OMECER 10MG CAPSULE contains Omeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called  Proton pump inhibitors. It is used in the management of gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (acid contents in the stomach flow back into the tube connecting your mouth and stomach causing heartburn, nausea, vomiting, bitter taste and discomfort in the upper abdomen) in children (above 1 year of age) and adults.

It is used in adults to manage gastric (stomach), duodenal ulcers (upper part of the intestine), ulcers infected with Helicobacter pylori bacteria in addition to antibiotics (including children) and ulcers due to the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).

Also, it is used in adults to manage Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (increased acid secretion in the stomach due to growth in the pancreas resulting in abdominal pain, diarrhoea, gnawing or discomfort in the upper abdomen, heartburn, nausea and vomiting).

OMECER 10MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients with history of allergic reactions to omeprazole or any other proton pump inhibitors (Ex. pantoprazole, lansoprazole, rabeprazole and esomeprazole).

Before taking OMECER 10MG CAPSULE, tell your doctor if you have any severe liver problems, weight loss, swallowing problems, stomach pain or indigestion, osteoporosis (a condition in which bones become weak and brittle), vitamin B12 deficiency, schedule for a specific blood test (chromogranin A).

OMECER 10MG CAPSULE can be used in pregnant and breastfeeding women only if advised by the doctor. OMECER 10MG CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged above 65 years) due to the increased risk of fractures.

The most common side effects of taking OMECER 10MG CAPSULE are headache, diarrhoea, stomach pain, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects bother you.

introduction:
Introduction About O MACC DSR CAPSULE

O MACC DSR CAPSULE is a combination of Domperidone and Esomeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic Drugs and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. It is used in adults to manage peptic ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid). O MACC DSR CAPSULE acts by reducing the production of gastric acid. It also speeds up the movement of food from the stomach to the intestines, thereby reducing the signs of nausea, vomiting and acid reflux. Due to these actions, it can also reduce the unpleasant signs of GI tract such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion, burping, bloating, acidity or heartburn.

O MACC DSR CAPSULE is effective in managing peptic ulcer caused either due to stomach infection (H. pylori infection) or due to prolong use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (such as ibuprofen, Aceclofenac etc). It can also be used to manage re-bleeding from the ulcers. GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the acid from the stomach frequently flows into the esophagus leading to irritation of lining of food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

O MACC DSR CAPSULE should be taken at least 30 minutes before meals. During management with O MACC DSR CAPSULE your doctor will closely monitor your kidney functions, liver functions and blood magnesium levels to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before taking O MACC DSR CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any blockage or tears in the gut or have weak bones. O MACC DSR CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients having bleeding from the gut. Consult your doctor before taking O MACC DSR CAPSULE if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. The most common side effects of taking O MACC DSR CAPSULE are dryness of mouth, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect bothers you.

mechanismOfAction:
How O MACC DSR CAPSULE Works

O MACC DSR CAPSULE contains two medicines namely Domperidone and Esomeprazole. Domperidone works by blocking the actions of a chemical messenger called dopamine in the gut and across the brain and spinal cord. This action stimulates the gut, reduces acid reflux and speeds up the movements of food from the stomach into the intestines. It also blocks the transmission of nerve signals between the vomiting centers and the brain which reduces the onset of nausea and vomiting. Esomeprazole reduces gastric acid secretion by the blocking the actions of a protein membrane called H+K+Atpase (proton pump) present in the lining of the stomach. By reducing stomach acid production, O MACC DSR CAPSULE manages the worsening of ulcers, heals the existing ulcers and esophageal lesions and provides relief from the unpleasant symptoms of GI tract (such as acidity, bloating, burping and indigestion).

Do not stop taking O MACC DSR CAPSULE unless your doctor advice you to stop.

introduction:
Introduction About RABEMAC LS CAPSULE

RABEMAC LS CAPSULE is a combination of Levosulpiride and Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Dopamine D2 antagonists and Proton-pump inhibitors respectively. RABEMAC LS CAPSULE is indicated for the management of Gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD). GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the esophagus leading to irritation and inflammation of lining of food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

RABEMAC LS CAPSULE can also be used to manage peptic ulcer (painful sores in the gut), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid), functional dyspepsia (recurrent signs and symptoms of indigestion without an obvious cause) and diabetic gastroparesis (delayed gastric emptying caused due to diabetes).

Take RABEMAC LS CAPSULE preferably on an empty stomach. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking RABEMAC LS CAPSULE as it could potentiate the CNS depressive side effects.

Patients receiving long-term management (>1 year) with RABEMAC LS CAPSULE should be kept on regular surveillance because it can increase the risk of bone fracture (i.e., in the hip, wrist or spine) which is more predominant in the patients having osteoporosis or taking corticosteroids.

Before taking RABEMAC LS CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you have any heart, kidney or liver disease as a precaution. RABEMAC LS CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant or breastfeeding women, including children and adolescents (aged below 18 years).

The most common side effects of taking RABEMAC LS CAPSULE are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation and headache. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsen.

How RABEMAC LS CAPSULE Works

RABEMAC LS CAPSULE reduces stomach ulcers, nausea and acid reflux, where rabeprazole acts by inhibiting the secretions of stomach acid by blocking the proton pump (H+ K+ ATPase) at the secretory surface of gastric parietal cells and levosulpiride acts by blocking the dopamine D2 receptors in the CTZ (area in medulla oblongata that causes vomiting when stimulated) and in the gut, thus facilitating the movement of food from the stomach into the intestines followed by healing of ulcers or inflammatory lesions in the stomach and in the esophagus.

Others

RABEMAC LS CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you have:

Parkinson’s disease
History of epilepsy
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (a CNS disorder characterized by high fever, stiffness of the muscles, altered mental status (paranoid behavior) and autonomic dysfunction)
Breast cancer (with high levels of prolactin in the body)

Before taking RABEMAC LS CAPSULE, inform your physician if you: 

Have a tumor in the stomach or breast
Have bleeding or perforation of the gastrointestinal tract
Have or at risk of developing vitamin-B12 deficiency
Had developed any skin reaction following management with similar medicines that can reduce stomach acid
Are due to have a specific blood test (Chromogranin A)
Have osteoporosis
Are a smoker
Have porphyria (a rare blood disorder)
Have alcohol intoxication (drinking large amount of alcohol in short period)
Have or had phaeochromocytoma (tumors of adrenal gland) in the past
Have or had prolactinoma (a noncancerous tumor of pituitary gland) in the past
Have hypokalemia (decreased potassium levels in blood)
Have neuroendocrine tumor (tumors in neuroendocrine cells)
Have mania or other mental disorders
Have painful breasts

Use in pediatrics:

RABEMAC LS CAPSULE is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years). Consult your doctor before taking RABEMAC LS CAPSULE.

Use in geriatrics:

RABEMAC LS CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years or above). Consult your doctor before taking RABEMAC LS CAPSULE. Proper dose adjustments and careful monitoring are required in such patients.

introduction:
Introduction About PANTODAC DSR CAPSULE

PANTODAC DSR CAPSULE is used to manage peptic ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reflux esophagitis. It is a combination of Domperidone and Pantoprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic Drugs and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. PANTODAC DSR CAPSULE acts by reducing the production of gastric acid. It also speeds up the movement of food from the stomach to the intestines, thereby reducing the signs of nausea, vomiting and acid reflux. Due to these actions, it can also reduce the unpleasant signs of GI tract such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion, burping, bloating, acidity or heartburn.

It should be taken at least 15-30 minutes before meals. During management with PANTODAC DSR CAPSULE your doctor will closely monitor your kidney functions, liver functions and blood magnesium levels to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects. Before taking PANTODAC DSR CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any blockage or tears in the gut or have weak bones.

PANTODAC DSR CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients bleeding from the gut. Consult your doctor before taking PANTODAC DSR CAPSULE if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. The most common side effects are dryness of mouth, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect bothers you. You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience any signs of low magnesium levels in blood (such as tiredness, abnormal muscle movements, dizziness, confusion, disorientation, irregular heartbeat).

mechanismOfAction:
How PANTODAC DSR CAPSULE Works

PANTODAC DSR CAPSULE contains Domperidone and Pantoprazole. Domperidone is a prokinetic medicine with anti-emetic properties which works by blocking the actions of a chemical messenger called dopamine in the gut and across the brain and spinal cord. This action stimulates the gut, reduces acid reflux and speeds up the movements of food from the stomach into the intestines. It also blocks the transmission of nerve signals between the vomiting centers and brain which reduces the onset of nausea and vomiting. Pantoprazole reduces gastric acid secretion by the blocking the actions of a protein membrane called H+K+Atpase (proton pump) present in the lining of the stomach. By reducing stomach acid production, PANTODAC DSR CAPSULE it manages the worsening of ulcers, heals the existing ulcers and esophageal lesions and provides relief from the unpleasant symptoms of GI tract (such as acidity, bloating, burping and indigestion).

PANTODAC DSR CAPSULE does not affect your ability in driving or handling heavy tools or machines. However, do not drive or handle heavy tools or machines if your ability is affected by the medicine.

introduction:
Introduction About PANTOTAB 40 TABLET

PANTOTAB 40 TABLET contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking PANTOTAB 40 TABLET as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking PANTOTAB 40 TABLET, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How PANTOTAB 40 TABLET Works

PANTOTAB 40 TABLET contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why PANTOTAB 40 TABLET Is Effective for Acid Control:
PANTOTAB 40 TABLET effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take PANTOTAB 40 TABLET?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

More Information
01.What makes PANTOTAB 40 TABLET a preferred choice over other medications?
Potent and Long-Lasting Acid Suppression: PANTOTAB 40 TABLET contains pantoprazole, a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that effectively blocks the final step of stomach acid production, providing stronger and longer-lasting relief from symptoms like heartburn, acid reflux, and indigestion compared to H2 blockers or antacids.
Comprehensive Symptom Relief and Healing: It not only relieves discomfort from acid-related conditions but also promotes healing of stomach and duodenal ulcers, and helps manage more severe conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
Lowering with Painkiller Use: PANTOTAB 40 TABLET is recommended for lowering stomach ulcers and acidity in patients who require long-term use of painkillers (NSAIDs), a benefit not offered by all acid-reducing medicines.
Convenient Once-Daily Dosing: Its long duration of action allows for once-daily dosing, making it easier for patients to adhere to treatment and maintain consistent acid control.
Favorable Tolerability Profile: Most side effects are mild and temporary, such as headache, nausea, or diarrhea. Serious side effects are rare when used as directed, and the risk of complications can be minimized with appropriate monitoring.
Well-Studied and Trusted: Pantoprazole, the active ingredient, is widely used and supported by extensive clinical experience, ensuring both efficacy and safety for a broad range of patients.

These advantages make PANTOTAB 40 TABLET a reliable and effective option for both short-term relief and long-term management of acid-related disorders, often outperforming less potent or shorter-acting alternatives.

introduction:
Introduction About ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE

ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE is a combination of Domperidone and Esomeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic Drugs and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. It is used in adults to manage peptic ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid). ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE acts by reducing the production of gastric acid. It also speeds up the movement of food from the stomach to the intestines, thereby reducing the signs of nausea, vomiting and acid reflux. Due to these actions, it can also reduce the unpleasant signs of GI tract such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion, burping, bloating, acidity or heartburn.

ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE is effective in managing peptic ulcer caused either due to stomach infection (H. pylori infection) or due to prolong use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (such as ibuprofen, Aceclofenac etc). It can also be used to manage re-bleeding from the ulcers. GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the acid from the stomach frequently flows into the esophagus leading to irritation of lining of food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE should be taken at least 30 minutes before meals. During management with ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE your doctor will closely monitor your kidney functions, liver functions and blood magnesium levels to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before taking ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any blockage or tears in the gut or have weak bones. ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients having bleeding from the gut. Consult your doctor before taking ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. The most common side effects of taking ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE are dryness of mouth, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect bothers you.

mechanismOfAction:
How ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE Works

ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE contains two medicines namely Domperidone and Esomeprazole. Domperidone works by blocking the actions of a chemical messenger called dopamine in the gut and across the brain and spinal cord. This action stimulates the gut, reduces acid reflux and speeds up the movements of food from the stomach into the intestines. It also blocks the transmission of nerve signals between the vomiting centers and the brain which reduces the onset of nausea and vomiting. Esomeprazole reduces gastric acid secretion by the blocking the actions of a protein membrane called H+K+Atpase (proton pump) present in the lining of the stomach. By reducing stomach acid production, ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE manages the worsening of ulcers, heals the existing ulcers and esophageal lesions and provides relief from the unpleasant symptoms of GI tract (such as acidity, bloating, burping and indigestion).

Take ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE 30 minutes to 1 hour before meals or as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition. Do not stop taking ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE unless your doctor advice you to stop.

ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE may pass through breast milk. Therefore, it is not recommended for use in breastfeeding women unless considered necessary by the physician.

ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE does not affect your ability in driving or handling heavy tools or machines. However, do not drive or handle heavy tools or machines if your ability is affected by ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE.
Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE, as it could aggravate your existing condition.
ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.

ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients with moderate or severe liver impairment. It should be used with caution in patients with other mild liver problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.
Do not take ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE if you are allergic to Domperidone, Esomeprazole or to any other proton pump inhibitors (such as rabeprazole, pantoprazole).

ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients having heart problems (such as prolongation of QT wave, congestive heart failure or arrhythmia). Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.
ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) due to lack of safety data. However, consult your doctor before taking it.
ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years and above). Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.

Others

ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you:

Have bloody stools or bleeding in the gut
Have blockage or tear in the intestines
Have severe fluid or electrolyte disturbances
Have prolactinoma (a non-cancerous tumor of pituitary gland)
Have low blood potassium or magnesium levels
Have hyperkalemia (high blood potassium levels)

Before taking ESOZ D 20 CAPSULE inform your doctor if you:

Have osteoporosis
Have vitamin B12 deficiency (sore tongue, mouth ulcers, pale skin, depression)
Are going to test Chromogranin A level

Introduction About NEXPRO JUNIOR SACHET

NEXPRO JUNIOR SACHET contains Esomeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Proton pump inhibitors. It is used for the management of Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) heartburn in children aged above 1 year. NEXPRO JUNIOR SACHET also helps in managing ulcers in the stomach or upper part of the gut (intestine) that are infected with Helicobacter pylori bacteria in children above 4 years of age.

Antibiotics are usually prescribed along with this medicine for the ulcers to heal in such bacterial infections.

GERD is a disease where acid from the stomach escapes into the tube which connects your throat to your stomach (oesophagus) causing pain and inflammation.

NEXPRO JUNIOR SACHET should be taken in caution in patients with severe kidney and liver failure. NEXPRO JUNIOR SACHET should be taken only if considered clearly necessary by your doctor in pregnant women. It is not recommended for use in breast-feeding women. Consult your doctor before taking the medicine.

Before taking NEXPRO JUNIOR SACHET, inform your doctor if you have or ever had a skin reaction after taking medicine to manage acidity or have osteoporosis or are taking corticosteroids medication (increased risk of osteoporosis) or having any intolerance to sugars.

It is not recommended for use in children aged less than 1 year. The most common side effects of taking NEXPRO JUNIOR SACHET are headache, diarrhoea, stomach pain, constipation, flatulence, nausea and vomiting. Contact your physician if any of the above symptoms worsens with time.

introduction:
Introduction About PANTAKIND TABLET

PANTAKIND TABLET contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking PANTAKIND TABLET as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking PANTAKIND TABLET, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How PANTAKIND TABLET Works

PANTAKIND TABLET contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why PANTAKIND TABLET Is Effective for Acid Control:
PANTAKIND TABLET effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take PANTAKIND TABLET?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

More Information
01.What makes PANTAKIND TABLET a preferred choice over other medications?
Potent and Long-Lasting Acid Suppression: PANTAKIND TABLET contains pantoprazole, a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that effectively blocks the final step of stomach acid production, providing stronger and longer-lasting relief from symptoms like heartburn, acid reflux, and indigestion compared to H2 blockers or antacids.
Comprehensive Symptom Relief and Healing: It not only relieves discomfort from acid-related conditions but also promotes healing of stomach and duodenal ulcers, and helps manage more severe conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
Lowering with Painkiller Use: PANTAKIND TABLET is recommended for lowering stomach ulcers and acidity in patients who require long-term use of painkillers (NSAIDs), a benefit not offered by all acid-reducing medicines.
Convenient Once-Daily Dosing: Its long duration of action allows for once-daily dosing, making it easier for patients to adhere to treatment and maintain consistent acid control.
Favorable Tolerability Profile: Most side effects are mild and temporary, such as headache, nausea, or diarrhea. Serious side effects are rare when used as directed, and the risk of complications can be minimized with appropriate monitoring.
Well-Studied and Trusted: Pantoprazole, the active ingredient, is widely used and supported by extensive clinical experience, ensuring both efficacy and safety for a broad range of patients.

These advantages make PANTAKIND TABLET a reliable and effective option for both short-term relief and long-term management of acid-related disorders, often outperforming less potent or shorter-acting alternatives.

introduction:
Introduction About PROTERA D CAPSULE

PROTERA D CAPSULE is used to manage peptic ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reflux esophagitis. It is a combination of Domperidone and Pantoprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic Drugs and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. PROTERA D CAPSULE acts by reducing the production of gastric acid. It also speeds up the movement of food from the stomach to the intestines, thereby reducing the signs of nausea, vomiting and acid reflux. Due to these actions, it can also reduce the unpleasant signs of GI tract such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion, burping, bloating, acidity or heartburn.

It should be taken at least 15-30 minutes before meals. During management with PROTERA D CAPSULE your doctor will closely monitor your kidney functions, liver functions and blood magnesium levels to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects. Before taking PROTERA D CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any blockage or tears in the gut or have weak bones.

PROTERA D CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients bleeding from the gut. Consult your doctor before taking PROTERA D CAPSULE if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. The most common side effects are dryness of mouth, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect bothers you. You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience any signs of low magnesium levels in blood (such as tiredness, abnormal muscle movements, dizziness, confusion, disorientation, irregular heartbeat).

mechanismOfAction:
How PROTERA D CAPSULE Works

PROTERA D CAPSULE contains Domperidone and Pantoprazole. Domperidone is a prokinetic medicine with anti-emetic properties which works by blocking the actions of a chemical messenger called dopamine in the gut and across the brain and spinal cord. This action stimulates the gut, reduces acid reflux and speeds up the movements of food from the stomach into the intestines. It also blocks the transmission of nerve signals between the vomiting centers and brain which reduces the onset of nausea and vomiting. Pantoprazole reduces gastric acid secretion by the blocking the actions of a protein membrane called H+K+Atpase (proton pump) present in the lining of the stomach. By reducing stomach acid production, PROTERA D CAPSULE it manages the worsening of ulcers, heals the existing ulcers and esophageal lesions and provides relief from the unpleasant symptoms of GI tract (such as acidity, bloating, burping and indigestion).

introduction:
Introduction About PANPLUS 40MG TABLET

PANPLUS 40MG TABLET contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking PANPLUS 40MG TABLET as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking PANPLUS 40MG TABLET, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How PANPLUS 40MG TABLET Works

PANPLUS 40MG TABLET contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why PANPLUS 40MG TABLET Is Effective for Acid Control:
PANPLUS 40MG TABLET effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take PANPLUS 40MG TABLET?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

More Information
01.What makes PANPLUS 40MG TABLET a preferred choice over other medications?
Potent and Long-Lasting Acid Suppression: PANPLUS 40MG TABLET contains pantoprazole, a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that effectively blocks the final step of stomach acid production, providing stronger and longer-lasting relief from symptoms like heartburn, acid reflux, and indigestion compared to H2 blockers or antacids.
Comprehensive Symptom Relief and Healing: It not only relieves discomfort from acid-related conditions but also promotes healing of stomach and duodenal ulcers, and helps manage more severe conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
Lowering with Painkiller Use: PANPLUS 40MG TABLET is recommended for lowering stomach ulcers and acidity in patients who require long-term use of painkillers (NSAIDs), a benefit not offered by all acid-reducing medicines.
Convenient Once-Daily Dosing: Its long duration of action allows for once-daily dosing, making it easier for patients to adhere to treatment and maintain consistent acid control.
Favorable Tolerability Profile: Most side effects are mild and temporary, such as headache, nausea, or diarrhea. Serious side effects are rare when used as directed, and the risk of complications can be minimized with appropriate monitoring.
Well-Studied and Trusted: Pantoprazole, the active ingredient, is widely used and supported by extensive clinical experience, ensuring both efficacy and safety for a broad range of patients.

These advantages make PANPLUS 40MG TABLET a reliable and effective option for both short-term relief and long-term management of acid-related disorders, often outperforming less potent or shorter-acting alternatives.

name: Odirab 20mg Tablet 10'S
introduction:
Introduction About ODIRAB 20MG TABLET

ODIRAB 20MG TABLET contains Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Proton pump inhibitors. It is used to manage Gastro-esophageal Reflux Disease (GERD), peptic ulcer and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumours in the pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid).

GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the oesophagus leading to the irritation of lining of the food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

Peptic ulcers are painful sores that develop on the linings of the stomach, oesophagus and/or intestines. Symptoms include stomach pain, flatulence, indigestion, vomiting and fatigue.

Take ODIRAB 20MG TABLET preferably before meals or as directed by the physician. Before taking ODIRAB 20MG TABLET inform your doctor if you have any liver problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have vitamin B12 deficiency, osteoporosis or any tumors in your stomach.

Do not take ODIRAB 20MG TABLET if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without consulting your doctor. The most common side effects of taking ODIRAB 20MG TABLET are oral sores, constipation, indigestion, stomach pain, headache and dizziness. Consult your doctor if any of the side effect troubles you.

You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience severe uncontrollable diarrhea with stomach pain or tenderness after taking ODIRAB 20MG TABLET.

introduction:
Introduction About SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE

SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE is a combination of Levosulpiride and Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Dopamine D2 antagonists and Proton-pump inhibitors respectively. SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE is indicated for the management of Gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD). GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the esophagus leading to irritation and inflammation of lining of food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE can also be used to manage peptic ulcer (painful sores in the gut), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid), functional dyspepsia (recurrent signs and symptoms of indigestion without an obvious cause) and diabetic gastroparesis (delayed gastric emptying caused due to diabetes).

Take SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE preferably on an empty stomach. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE as it could potentiate the CNS depressive side effects.

Patients receiving long-term management (>1 year) with SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE should be kept on regular surveillance because it can increase the risk of bone fracture (i.e., in the hip, wrist or spine) which is more predominant in the patients having osteoporosis or taking corticosteroids.

Before taking SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you have any heart, kidney or liver disease as a precaution. SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant or breastfeeding women, including children and adolescents (aged below 18 years).

The most common side effects of taking SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation and headache. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsen.

mechanismOfAction:
How SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE Works

SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE reduces stomach ulcers, nausea and acid reflux, where rabeprazole acts by inhibiting the secretions of stomach acid by blocking the proton pump (H+ K+ ATPase) at the secretory surface of gastric parietal cells and levosulpiride acts by blocking the dopamine D2 receptors in the CTZ (area in medulla oblongata that causes vomiting when stimulated) and in the gut, thus facilitating the movement of food from the stomach into the intestines followed by healing of ulcers or inflammatory lesions in the stomach and in the esophagus.

History of epilepsy

Have a tumor in the stomach or breast
Have bleeding or perforation of the gastrointestinal tract
Have or at risk of developing vitamin-B12 deficiency
Had developed any skin reaction following management with similar medicines that can reduce stomach acid
Are due to have a specific blood test (Chromogranin A)

Are a smoker

Have alcohol intoxication (drinking large amount of alcohol in short period)

Have painful breasts

Use in geriatrics:

SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years or above). Consult your doctor before taking SULGIRIDE R CAPSULE. Proper dose adjustments and careful monitoring are required in such patients.

introduction:
Introduction About BICARCID 500 TABLET

BICARCID 500 Tablet is an alkalizing agent that is used in the management of metabolic acidosis, promotion of gastric, systemic, and urinary alkalinization and used as a replacement therapy in severe diarrhea. It contains sodium bicarbonate as the active ingredient.

Sodium Bicarbonate works by increasing the pH of blood and urine, thereby correcting metabolic acidosis (high levels of acid in the blood). In case of excessive fluid loss (such as in diarrhea), it works by replenishing salt and electrolyte levels.

Take BICARCID 500 Tablet as advised by your doctor. Swallow the tablet with a glass of water and do not crush or chew the tablet. Do not exceed the recommended daily dosage.

introduction:
Introduction About PANTIN D CAPSULE

PANTIN D CAPSULE is used to manage peptic ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reflux esophagitis. It is a combination of Domperidone and Pantoprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic Drugs and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. PANTIN D CAPSULE acts by reducing the production of gastric acid. It also speeds up the movement of food from the stomach to the intestines, thereby reducing the signs of nausea, vomiting and acid reflux. Due to these actions, it can also reduce the unpleasant signs of GI tract such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion, burping, bloating, acidity or heartburn.

It should be taken at least 15-30 minutes before meals. During management with PANTIN D CAPSULE your doctor will closely monitor your kidney functions, liver functions and blood magnesium levels to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects. Before taking PANTIN D CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any blockage or tears in the gut or have weak bones.

PANTIN D CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients bleeding from the gut. Consult your doctor before taking PANTIN D CAPSULE if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. The most common side effects are dryness of mouth, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect bothers you. You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience any signs of low magnesium levels in blood (such as tiredness, abnormal muscle movements, dizziness, confusion, disorientation, irregular heartbeat).

mechanismOfAction:
How PANTIN D CAPSULE Works

PANTIN D CAPSULE contains Domperidone and Pantoprazole. Domperidone is a prokinetic medicine with anti-emetic properties which works by blocking the actions of a chemical messenger called dopamine in the gut and across the brain and spinal cord. This action stimulates the gut, reduces acid reflux and speeds up the movements of food from the stomach into the intestines. It also blocks the transmission of nerve signals between the vomiting centers and brain which reduces the onset of nausea and vomiting. Pantoprazole reduces gastric acid secretion by the blocking the actions of a protein membrane called H+K+Atpase (proton pump) present in the lining of the stomach. By reducing stomach acid production, PANTIN D CAPSULE it manages the worsening of ulcers, heals the existing ulcers and esophageal lesions and provides relief from the unpleasant symptoms of GI tract (such as acidity, bloating, burping and indigestion).

introduction:
Introduction About RABEMAC DSR CAPSULE

RABEMAC DSR CAPSULE is used to manage Gastro-Esophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) among patients who have not responded adequately to rabeprazole alone. It is a combination of Domperidone and Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Dopamine Antagonists and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. It can also be used to manage peptic ulcers caused by H. pylori infection or NSAIDs use.

Along management with RABEMAC DSR CAPSULE, try to eat less spicy foods and drink plenty of water. Avoid smoking or alcohol consumption as it may aggravate your existing condition. Patients receiving long-term management with the medicine should be kept on regular surveillance to rule out the risk of hypomagnesaemia (decreased magnesium levels in blood) and bone fracture, predominantly in the elderly patients and in patients with other recognized risk factors.

Before taking RABEMAC DSR CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. Your doctor may reduce the dose or suggest an alternative therapy. It is not recommended for use in pregnant or breastfeeding women and in children (aged less than 18 years). It should be used with caution in elderly patients (above 65 years of age). The most common side effects are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea or constipation. Consult your doctor if any of these above side effects worsen.

name: Rekool L 40mg Tablet 10'S
introduction:
Introduction About REKOOL L 40MG TABLET

REKOOL L 40MG TABLET is a combination of Levosulpiride and Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Dopamine D2 antagonists and Proton-pump inhibitors respectively. REKOOL L 40MG TABLET is indicated for the management of Gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD). GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the esophagus leading to irritation and inflammation of lining of food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

REKOOL L 40MG TABLET can also be used to manage peptic ulcer (painful sores in the gut), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid), functional dyspepsia (recurrent signs and symptoms of indigestion without an obvious cause) and diabetic gastroparesis (delayed gastric emptying caused due to diabetes).

Take REKOOL L 40MG TABLET preferably on an empty stomach. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking REKOOL L 40MG TABLET as it could potentiate the CNS depressive side effects.

Patients receiving long-term management (>1 year) with REKOOL L 40MG TABLET should be kept on regular surveillance because it can increase the risk of bone fracture (i.e., in the hip, wrist or spine) which is more predominant in the patients having osteoporosis or taking corticosteroids.

Before taking REKOOL L 40MG TABLET, inform your doctor if you have any heart, kidney or liver disease as a precaution. REKOOL L 40MG TABLET is not recommended for use in pregnant or breastfeeding women, including children and adolescents (aged below 18 years).

The most common side effects of taking REKOOL L 40MG TABLET are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation and headache. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsen.
usesDetails:
Uses Of REKOOL L 40MG TABLET
Manage Gastro-Esophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
Manage function dyspepsia
Manage peptic ulcer
Manage Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
Manage diabetic gastroparesis
mechanismOfAction:
How REKOOL L 40MG TABLET Works

REKOOL L 40MG TABLET reduces stomach ulcers, nausea and acid reflux, where rabeprazole acts by inhibiting the secretions of stomach acid by blocking the proton pump (H+ K+ ATPase) at the secretory surface of gastric parietal cells and levosulpiride acts by blocking the dopamine D2 receptors in the CTZ (area in medulla oblongata that causes vomiting when stimulated) and in the gut, thus facilitating the movement of food from the stomach into the intestines followed by healing of ulcers or inflammatory lesions in the stomach and in the esophagus.

Take REKOOL L 40MG TABLET on an empty stomach or as advised by your physician. Swallow REKOOL L 40MG TABLET as a whole and do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

REKOOL L 40MG TABLET should be taken with caution in patients with kidney disease. Consult your doctor before taking REKOOL L 40MG TABLET.
REKOOL L 40MG TABLET should be taken with caution in patients with a previous history of liver problems. Consult your doctor before taking REKOOL L 40MG TABLET.
Do not take REKOOL L 40MG TABLET if you are allergic to Levosulpiride, Rabeprazole or other proton-pump inhibitors (Ex. pantoprazole, omeprazole, lansoprazole).
REKOOL L 40MG TABLET should be taken with caution in patients with asthma or other respiratory diseases. Consult your doctor before taking REKOOL L 40MG TABLET.
REKOOL L 40MG TABLET should be taken with caution in patients with heart disease. Consult your doctor before taking REKOOL L 40MG TABLET.

Others

REKOOL L 40MG TABLET is not recommended for use if you have:

Parkinson’s disease
History of epilepsy
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (a CNS disorder characterized by high fever, stiffness of the muscles, altered mental status (paranoid behavior) and autonomic dysfunction)
Breast cancer (with high levels of prolactin in the body)

Before taking REKOOL L 40MG TABLET, inform your physician if you: 

Have a tumor in the stomach or breast
Have bleeding or perforation of the gastrointestinal tract
Have or at risk of developing vitamin-B12 deficiency
Had developed any skin reaction following management with similar medicines that can reduce stomach acid
Are due to have a specific blood test (Chromogranin A)
Have osteoporosis
Are a smoker
Have porphyria (a rare blood disorder)
Have alcohol intoxication (drinking large amount of alcohol in short period)
Have or had phaeochromocytoma (tumors of adrenal gland) in the past
Have or had prolactinoma (a noncancerous tumor of pituitary gland) in the past
Have hypokalemia (decreased potassium levels in blood)
Have neuroendocrine tumor (tumors in neuroendocrine cells)
Have mania or other mental disorders
Have painful breasts

Use in pediatrics:

REKOOL L 40MG TABLET is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years). Consult your doctor before taking REKOOL L 40MG TABLET.

Use in geriatrics:

REKOOL L 40MG TABLET should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years or above). Consult your doctor before taking REKOOL L 40MG TABLET. Proper dose adjustments and careful monitoring are required in such patients.

introduction:
Introduction About JOPAN DSR CAPSULE

JOPAN DSR CAPSULE is used to manage peptic ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reflux esophagitis. It is a combination of Domperidone and Pantoprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic Drugs and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. JOPAN DSR CAPSULE acts by reducing the production of gastric acid. It also speeds up the movement of food from the stomach to the intestines, thereby reducing the signs of nausea, vomiting and acid reflux. Due to these actions, it can also reduce the unpleasant signs of GI tract such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion, burping, bloating, acidity or heartburn.

It should be taken at least 15-30 minutes before meals. During management with JOPAN DSR CAPSULE your doctor will closely monitor your kidney functions, liver functions and blood magnesium levels to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects. Before taking JOPAN DSR CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any blockage or tears in the gut or have weak bones.

JOPAN DSR CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients bleeding from the gut. Consult your doctor before taking JOPAN DSR CAPSULE if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. The most common side effects are dryness of mouth, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect bothers you. You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience any signs of low magnesium levels in blood (such as tiredness, abnormal muscle movements, dizziness, confusion, disorientation, irregular heartbeat).

mechanismOfAction:
How JOPAN DSR CAPSULE Works

JOPAN DSR CAPSULE contains Domperidone and Pantoprazole. Domperidone is a prokinetic medicine with anti-emetic properties which works by blocking the actions of a chemical messenger called dopamine in the gut and across the brain and spinal cord. This action stimulates the gut, reduces acid reflux and speeds up the movements of food from the stomach into the intestines. It also blocks the transmission of nerve signals between the vomiting centers and brain which reduces the onset of nausea and vomiting. Pantoprazole reduces gastric acid secretion by the blocking the actions of a protein membrane called H+K+Atpase (proton pump) present in the lining of the stomach. By reducing stomach acid production, JOPAN DSR CAPSULE it manages the worsening of ulcers, heals the existing ulcers and esophageal lesions and provides relief from the unpleasant symptoms of GI tract (such as acidity, bloating, burping and indigestion).

JOPAN DSR CAPSULE does not affect your ability in driving or handling heavy tools or machines. However, do not drive or handle heavy tools or machines if your ability is affected by the medicine.

introduction:
Introduction About LEVOGASTROL OD TABLET

 

LEVOGASTROL OD TABLET contains Levosulpiride, which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic agents. It is used to manage nausea, vomiting, and indigestion. It can also be used to manage diabetic gastroparesis.

Diabetic gastroparesis is a stomach condition caused by poorly controlled diabetes. It manages the stomach muscles from emptying their digested contents into the intestines. This creates a feeling of fullness even after eating only a little amount of food, along with nausea and a lack of appetite.

Before taking LEVOGASTROL OD TABLET, inform your doctor if you have any kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have epilepsy, mania, or any other mental illness as a precaution.

LEVOGASTROL OD TABLET is not recommended for use in patients having bleeding or any blockage or tear in the gut. It is also not suitable for use in patients having cancer or tumours in the body. Do not take LEVOGASTROL OD TABLET without consulting your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.

The most common side effects of taking LEVOGASTROL OD TABLET are headache, drowsiness, tiredness, breast enlargement and discharge, and a decrease in sex drive. Consult your doctor if any of these side effects bother you.

introduction:
Introduction About RABEMAC 20MG TABLET

RABEMAC 20MG TABLET contains Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Proton pump inhibitors. It is used to manage Gastro-esophageal Reflux Disease (GERD), peptic ulcer and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumours in the pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid).

GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the oesophagus leading to the irritation of lining of the food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

Peptic ulcers are painful sores that develop on the linings of the stomach, oesophagus and/or intestines. Symptoms include stomach pain, flatulence, indigestion, vomiting and fatigue.

Take RABEMAC 20MG TABLET preferably before meals or as directed by the physician. Before taking RABEMAC 20MG TABLET inform your doctor if you have any liver problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have vitamin B12 deficiency, osteoporosis or any tumors in your stomach.

Do not take RABEMAC 20MG TABLET if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without consulting your doctor. The most common side effects of taking RABEMAC 20MG TABLET are oral sores, constipation, indigestion, stomach pain, headache and dizziness. Consult your doctor if any of the side effect troubles you.

You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience severe uncontrollable diarrhea with stomach pain or tenderness after taking RABEMAC 20MG TABLET.
usesDetails:
Uses Of RABEMAC 20MG TABLET
Manage Gastro-Esophageal Reflux Disease
Manage and Manages Peptic ulcers
Manage Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
mechanismOfAction:
How RABEMAC 20MG TABLET Works

RABEMAC 20MG TABLET is a proton pump inhibitor. It reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach by blocking the actions of an enzyme called H+ K+ ATPase (also known as proton pump) which is present in the lining of the stomach walls. As a result, it reduces the chances for acid reflux into the oesophagus, heals peptic ulcers and esophageal lesions and manages its recurrence.
usageDetails:
How to use RABEMAC 20MG TABLET

Take RABEMAC 20MG TABLET as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. It is preferably taken in the mornings or at any time of the day before meals.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

name: Pantium L Capsule 10'S
introduction:
Introduction About PANTIUM L CAPSULE

PANTIUM L CAPSULE is a combination of Levosulpiride and Pantoprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Dopamine D2 antagonists and Proton-pump inhibitors respectively. PANTIUM L CAPSULE is indicated for the short-term management of gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD) among patients who do not respond adequately to proton-pump inhibitors (Ex. pantoprazole, omeprazole, rabeprazole) alone.

GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the esophagus leading to irritation and inflammation of lining of food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

PANTIUM L CAPSULE can also be used to manage peptic ulcer (painful sores in the gut) caused by H. pylori infection or NSAIDs use and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid).

Take PANTIUM L CAPSULE preferably one hour before meals. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE as it could potentiate the CNS depressive side effects.

Patients receiving long-term management with PANTIUM L CAPSULE should be kept on regular surveillance to rule out the risk of hypomagnesaemia (decreased magnesium levels in blood) and bone fracture, predominantly in the elderly patients and in patients with other recognized risk factors like osteoporosis. 

Before taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. PANTIUM L CAPSULE is generally not recommended for use in pregnant or breastfeeding women and in children or adolescents (below 18 years of age).

PANTIUM L CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years or above) due to increased risk of postural hypotension, sedation and extrapyramidal effects (such as involuntary muscle movements, restless, muscle stiffness).

The most common side effects of taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE are nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, polyps in the stomach gut and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects worsen during or after management with PANTIUM L CAPSULE.

mechanismOfAction:
How PANTIUM L CAPSULE Works

PANTIUM L CAPSULE reduces stomach ulcers and acid reflux, where pantoprazole acts by inhibiting the secretions of stomach acid by blocking the proton pump (H+ K+ ATPase) at the secretory surface of gastric parietal cells and levosulpiride acts by facilitating gastric emptying and bowel movements by blocking the dopamine D2 receptors in the gut, thus reducing acid reflux and healing of stomach ulcers and esophageal lesions.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of PANTIUM L CAPSULE for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition. Do not stop taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE without informing your doctor.

warnings.details: PANTIUM L CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant women. Consult your doctor before taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE.
PANTIUM L CAPSULE is not recommended for use in breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE.
Do not drive or operate any heavy tools or machines if you experience dizziness, drowsiness, involuntary muscle movements or blurred vision after taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE.
Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE, as it may cause additive sedative effects.
PANTIUM L CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients with severe impaired kidney function consult your doctor before taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE.

PANTIUM L CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients with severe impaired liver function and it should be used with caution in patients with mild to moderate severe hepatic cirrhosis. Consult your doctor before taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE.
Do not take PANTIUM L CAPSULE if you are allergic to Levosulpiride or Pantoprazole. Consult your doctor before taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE.
PANTIUM L CAPSULE should be taken with caution in patients with cardiovascular disease or a family history of prolonged QT interval. Consult your doctor before taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE.

Others

PANTIUM L CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you:

Have phaeochromocytoma (tumors of adrenal gland)
Have epilepsy
Have mania or other mental disorders
Have breast cancer or prolactinoma (a noncancerous tumor of pituitary gland)
Have gastrointestinal bleeding or obstruction in the gut 

Before taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE, inform your physician if you:

Have gastric malignancy (cancers in the gut)
Have or at risk of developing vitamin B12 deficiency
Are going to test Chromogranin A level
Have or at risk of having osteoporosis
Have a history of cerebrovascular events (stroke, venous thromboembolism)
Are alcoholic

Use in pediatrics:

PANTIUM L CAPSULE is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) due to lack of safety and efficacy data. Consult your child’s doctor for advice.

Use in geriatrics:

PANTIUM L CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years or above) due to increased risk of postural hypotension, sedation and extrapyramidal effects (such as involuntary muscle movements, restless, muscle stiffness). Consult your doctor before taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE. Dose should be adjusted in patients with evidence of impaired kidney function.

Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking PANTIUM L CAPSULE inform to your doctor, if you are taking any of these medicines:

Medicines used to manage fungal infections (such as ketoconazole, itraconazole or posaconazole, amphotericin B)
Erlotinib (used to manage certain types of cancer)
Warfarin and phenprocoumon (used to manage or manage thrombotic events and heart problems)
Medicines used to manage HIV infection (such as atazanavir)
Methotrexate (a medicine used to manage rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis or cancer)
Rifampicin (used to manage tuberculosis)
Erythromycin and ampicillin esters (used to manage bacterial infections) Ex. hetacillin and pivampicillin
Iron salts (used to manage anemia) Ex. ferrous sulphate, ferrous fumarate
Medicine that can neutralize stomach acid such as antacids (Ex. aluminium- and magnesium-hydroxide) or sucralfate
Anticholinergics (used to relax or reduce the movements of smooth muscles and suppresses body secretions (Ex. atropine, hyoscine)
Analgesics (used to relieve pain) such as opioids (Ex. methadone) or non-opioids (Ex. naproxen, ibuprofen)
Sedatives and hypnotics, tranquilizers (used to reduce anxiety and to induce sleep) Ex. alprazolam, chlordiazepoxide, diazepam
Medicines used to manage depression (Ex. rasagiline, selegiline, phenelzine, haloperidol, imipramine, lithium, fluvoxamine and herbal medicine (St. John’s wort))
Medicines used to manage abnormal heart rate (Ex. digitalis, quinine, quinidine, disopyramide, amiodarone, sotalol, flecainide, procainamide)
Medicines used to manage high blood pressure or other heart problems such as beta-blockers (Ex. propranolol, atenolol) or calcium channel blockers (Ex. verapamil, diltiazem)
Antipsychotics (used to manage mental illness) Ex. risperidone, paliperidone, amisulpiride, olanzapine, thioridazine
Non-sedating antihistamines (used to manage allergic symptoms) Ex. fexofenadine, levocetirizine, loratadine
Antimalarials (used to manage malaria) Ex. quinine, primaquine, halofantrine
Cisapride (used to manage heartburn and acid reflux)
Diuretics (used to reduce blood pressure by increasing urine output) Ex. spironolactone, chlorothiazide, acetazolamide
Corticosteroids (used to manage allergy, pain or inflammation) Ex. dexamethasone, prednisolone
Stimulant laxatives (used to manage constipation) Ex. bisacodyl
Pimozide (used to reduce uncontrollable muscle movements)
Pentamidine (used to manage lung infection)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally take too much of PANTIUM L CAPSULE, contact your doctor immediately or go to a hospital straight away. Overdosage symptoms of PANTIUM L CAPSULE might include extrapyramidal reactions (such as rigidity, tremor, drooling etc.) or sleep disturbances.

name: Acera 20mg Capsule 10'S
introduction:
Introduction About ACERA 20MG CAPSULE

ACERA 20MG CAPSULE contains Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Proton pump inhibitors. It is used to manage Gastro-esophageal Reflux Disease (GERD), peptic ulcer and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumours in the pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid).

GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the oesophagus leading to the irritation of lining of the food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

Peptic ulcers are painful sores that develop on the linings of the stomach, oesophagus and/or intestines. Symptoms include stomach pain, flatulence, indigestion, vomiting and fatigue.

Take ACERA 20MG CAPSULE preferably before meals or as directed by the physician. Before taking ACERA 20MG CAPSULE inform your doctor if you have any liver problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have vitamin B12 deficiency, osteoporosis or any tumors in your stomach.

Do not take ACERA 20MG CAPSULE if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without consulting your doctor. The most common side effects of taking ACERA 20MG CAPSULE are oral sores, constipation, indigestion, stomach pain, headache and dizziness. Consult your doctor if any of the side effect troubles you.

You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience severe uncontrollable diarrhea with stomach pain or tenderness after taking ACERA 20MG CAPSULE.
usesDetails:
Uses Of ACERA 20MG CAPSULE
Manage Gastro-Esophageal Reflux Disease
Manage and Manages Peptic ulcers
Manage Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
mechanismOfAction:
How ACERA 20MG CAPSULE Works

ACERA 20MG CAPSULE is a proton pump inhibitor. It reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach by blocking the actions of an enzyme called H+ K+ ATPase (also known as proton pump) which is present in the lining of the stomach walls. As a result, it reduces the chances for acid reflux into the oesophagus, heals peptic ulcers and esophageal lesions and manages its recurrence.
usageDetails:
How to use ACERA 20MG CAPSULE

Take ACERA 20MG CAPSULE as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. It is preferably taken in the mornings or at any time of the day before meals.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.
sideEffects: Stomach pain, diarrhoea, flatulence, nausea, vomiting or constipation
Fractures involving wrist, hip and spine
Allergic reactions (such as skin rash, itching, swelling of your face, difficulty in breathing and low blood pressure)
Skin rashes on sun exposed areas
Signs of frequent infections (such as chills, sore throat and fever)
Painful ulcers in the mouth or throat
Severe watery or bloody diarrhoea with fever, stomach pain or tenderness
Signs of vitamin B12 deficiency (such as pale skin, oral sores, disturbed vision, irritability, depression)

Common
Mouth sores
Difficulty in sleeping
Headache, dizziness
Stomach pain, diarrhoea, flatulence, nausea, vomiting or constipation
Aches or back pain
Polyps in the stomach
Uncommon

Bruising or bleeding easily
Severe watery or bloody diarrhoea with fever, stomach pain or tenderness
