warnings.details: ACERA 20MG CAPSULE is generally not recommended for use in pregnant women. Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.
ACERA 20MG CAPSULE is generally not recommended for use in breastfeeding women. Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.
Do not drive or operate any machines if you feel sleepy after taking ACERA 20MG CAPSULE.
ACERA 20MG CAPSULE should be used with caution in patients who have or ever had any liver problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.
Do not take ACERA 20MG CAPSULE if you are allergic to Rabeprazole or to any other proton pump inhibitors (such as omeprazole, esomeprazole).

Others

Before taking ACERA 20MG CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you:

Have a tumor in your stomach
Had a skin reaction after management with a medicine similar to ACERA 20MG CAPSULE
Have osteoporosis (weak bones)
Are going to have a specific blood test (Chromogranin A)

Use in pediatrics:

ACERA 20MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years). Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before administration.

 Use in geriatrics:

ACERA 20MG CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients. Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.

introduction:
Introduction About ULTRA MAGNESIUM 200MG TABLET

Ultra Magnesium Tablet is a nutrient supplement used to support energy release and reduction of tiredness and fatigue. It also supports the nervous system and muscle function, psychological function and maintenance of bones and teeth. It contains magnesium as an active ingredient.

Magnesium contributes to normal energy release and helps to reduce tiredness and fatigue. It contributes to normal functioning of the nervous system and has a role in the process of cell division, growth and maintenance of muscle mass and contributes to normal protein synthesis, as well as maintenance of normal bones and teeth and electrolyte balance.

Take Ultra Magnesium Tablet as advised by your doctor. Take 1 tablet daily after the main meal or as advised by your doctor. Swallow the medicine with water. Do not crush or chew the medicine.

introduction:
Introduction About ENLIVA CAPSULE

ENLIVA CAPSULE is a combination of Levosulpiride and Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Dopamine D2 antagonists and Proton-pump inhibitors respectively. ENLIVA CAPSULE is indicated for the management of Gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD). GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the esophagus leading to irritation and inflammation of lining of food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

ENLIVA CAPSULE can also be used to manage peptic ulcer (painful sores in the gut), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid), functional dyspepsia (recurrent signs and symptoms of indigestion without an obvious cause) and diabetic gastroparesis (delayed gastric emptying caused due to diabetes).

Take ENLIVA CAPSULE preferably on an empty stomach. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking ENLIVA CAPSULE as it could potentiate the CNS depressive side effects.

Patients receiving long-term management (>1 year) with ENLIVA CAPSULE should be kept on regular surveillance because it can increase the risk of bone fracture (i.e., in the hip, wrist or spine) which is more predominant in the patients having osteoporosis or taking corticosteroids.

Before taking ENLIVA CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you have any heart, kidney or liver disease as a precaution. ENLIVA CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant or breastfeeding women, including children and adolescents (aged below 18 years).

The most common side effects of taking ENLIVA CAPSULE are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation and headache. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsen.

mechanismOfAction:
How ENLIVA CAPSULE Works

ENLIVA CAPSULE reduces stomach ulcers, nausea and acid reflux, where rabeprazole acts by inhibiting the secretions of stomach acid by blocking the proton pump (H+ K+ ATPase) at the secretory surface of gastric parietal cells and levosulpiride acts by blocking the dopamine D2 receptors in the CTZ (area in medulla oblongata that causes vomiting when stimulated) and in the gut, thus facilitating the movement of food from the stomach into the intestines followed by healing of ulcers or inflammatory lesions in the stomach and in the esophagus.
usageDetails:
How to use ENLIVA CAPSULE

Take ENLIVA CAPSULE on an empty stomach or as advised by your physician. Swallow ENLIVA CAPSULE as a whole and do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

ENLIVA CAPSULE should be taken with caution in patients with a previous history of liver problems. Consult your doctor before taking ENLIVA CAPSULE.

ENLIVA CAPSULE should be taken with caution in patients with asthma or other respiratory diseases. Consult your doctor before taking ENLIVA CAPSULE.
ENLIVA CAPSULE should be taken with caution in patients with heart disease. Consult your doctor before taking ENLIVA CAPSULE.

Others

ENLIVA CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you have:

Parkinson’s disease
History of epilepsy
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (a CNS disorder characterized by high fever, stiffness of the muscles, altered mental status (paranoid behavior) and autonomic dysfunction)
Breast cancer (with high levels of prolactin in the body)

Before taking ENLIVA CAPSULE, inform your physician if you: 

Have a tumor in the stomach or breast
Have bleeding or perforation of the gastrointestinal tract
Have or at risk of developing vitamin-B12 deficiency
Had developed any skin reaction following management with similar medicines that can reduce stomach acid
Are due to have a specific blood test (Chromogranin A)
Have osteoporosis
Are a smoker
Have porphyria (a rare blood disorder)
Have alcohol intoxication (drinking large amount of alcohol in short period)
Have or had phaeochromocytoma (tumors of adrenal gland) in the past
Have or had prolactinoma (a noncancerous tumor of pituitary gland) in the past
Have hypokalemia (decreased potassium levels in blood)
Have neuroendocrine tumor (tumors in neuroendocrine cells)
Have mania or other mental disorders
Have painful breasts

Use in pediatrics:

ENLIVA CAPSULE is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years). Consult your doctor before taking ENLIVA CAPSULE.

Use in geriatrics:

ENLIVA CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years or above). Consult your doctor before taking ENLIVA CAPSULE. Proper dose adjustments and careful monitoring are required in such patients.

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking ENLIVA CAPSULE inform to your doctor, if you are taking any of these medicines:

Medicines used to manage HIV infection (Ex. atazanavir, nelfinavir, saquinavir, rilpivirine)
Antacids (used to neutralize stomach acid secretions) Ex. aluminium hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide
Sucralfate (used to manage duodenal ulcer)
Cisapride (used to manage heart burn in patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease)
Anticholinergics (medicines that causes smooth muscle relaxation and decreases body secretions) Ex. atropine, scopolamine, homatropine
Levodopa (used for parkinson’s disease)
Medicines causing low levels of potassium in blood such as furosemide (used to manage edema), corticosteroids (used to manage inflammation) Ex. cortisol, laxatives such as bisacodyl (used to manage constipation)
Iron salts (used to manage iron deficiency) Ex. ferrous sulphate, ferric ammonium citrate
Medicines used to manage high blood pressure and other heart problems (Ex. captopril, enalapril, losartan, valsartan, diltiazem, digoxin, quinidine)
Atomoxetine (used to manage attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder)
Terfenadine (used to manage allergic conditions)
Chloroquine (used to manage or manage malaria)
Clarithromycin or amoxicillin (used to manage bacterial infections)
Medicines used to manage cancer (Ex. erlotinib, dasatinib, nilotinib)
Methotrexate (used to manage cancer and auto-immune disease)
Tacrolimus or mycophenolate mofetil (used to manage organ rejection after transplant)
Ketoconazole, itraconazole (used to manage fungal infection)
Warfarin (used for blood thinning and management of heart problems)
Pregabalin (used to manage neuropathic pain)
Tramadol (used to manage pain)
Ipratropium (used to manage symptoms of COPD/asthma)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally take too much of ENLIVA CAPSULE, contact your doctor immediately or go to a hospital straight away.

introduction:
Introduction About ESOMAC L CAPSULE

ESOMAC L CAPSULE is a combination of Esomeprazole and Levosulpiride which belongs to the group of medicines called Proton-pump inhibitors and Dopamine D2 antagonists respectively. ESOMAC L CAPSULE is indicated for the management of Gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD) among patients who do not adequately respond to proton-pump inhibitors alone (Ex. pantoprazole, rabeprazole, esomeprazole, omeprazole).        

GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the esophagus leading to irritation of lining of food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.    

ESOMAC L CAPSULE can also be used to manage peptic ulcer caused by H. pylori infection or NSAID use. Peptic ulcers are painful sores that develop on the linings of the stomach, esophagus or intestines. Symptoms include stomach pain, flatulence, indigestion, vomiting and fatigue.   

Along management with ESOMAC L CAPSULE eat less spicy food and drink plenty of water or fluids as advised by your physician. Avoid consumption of alcohol as it could aggravate your existing disease conditions.   

Patients receiving long-term management with ESOMAC L CAPSULE should be kept on regular surveillance to rule out the risk of bone fractures (hip, wrist or spine), predominantly in patients taking corticosteroids and in patients with other recognized risk factors like osteoporosis. Before taking ESOMAC L CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you have any heart, kidney or liver disease as a precaution.  

ESOMAC L CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant or breastfeeding women, including children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) due to lack of safety and effectiveness.  ESOMAC L CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years or above).

The most common side effects of taking ESOMAC L CAPSULE are headache, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea or constipation. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects worsen.

Medicines used to manage HIV infection (Ex. nelfinavir, atazanavir)
Medicines used to manage fungal infections (Ex. ketoconazole, itraconazole or voriconazole)
Medicines used to manage depression (Ex. citalopram, imipramine, clomipramine, rasagiline, selegiline, phenelzine, or St. John’s wort)
Anticholinergics (used to reduce gastrointestinal movements) such as atropine, biperiden or hyoscine butylbromide
Narcotic analgesics (used to provide pain relief) Ex. morphine, pethidine, fentanyl

Clopidogrel (an antiplatelet medicine used to manage blood clots)
Erlotinib (used to manage cancer)
Phenytoin (used to manage epilepsy)
Medicines used for blood thinning (Ex. warfarin)

ESOMAC L CAPSULE can be taken with food or on an empty stomach. Try to take this medicine at least one hour before meals to maximize the efficacy. However, consult your doctor before taking ESOMAC L CAPSULE.

If you or anyone else accidentally take too much of ESOMAC L CAPSULE, contact your doctor immediately or go to a hospital straight away.

introduction:
Introduction About ESOBRINT 40 TABLET

ESOBRINT 40 TABLET, containing esomeprazole, is widely chosen by individuals seeking relief from persistent acidity, heartburn, and acid reflux symptoms. It is especially useful for those experiencing discomfort due to gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcers, erosive esophagitis, or conditions involving excessive stomach acid production such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. By blocking the proton pumps in the stomach lining, esomeprazole effectively reduces acid secretion, promoting healing of the stomach and esophageal lining and improving overall digestive comfort. 

This tablet is ideal for adults and can also be considered for use in elderly patients, pregnant or breastfeeding women, and those with kidney or liver conditions, though it should only be used under medical supervision in these groups. ESOBRINT 40 TABLET is generally taken once daily, preferably before meals, and should be swallowed whole with water—crushing or chewing the tablet is not recommended for optimal absorption. Consistency in timing and adherence to the prescribed duration are important for achieving the best results. 

Patients are advised to inform their healthcare provider about any existing allergies, liver problems, or plans for pregnancy or breastfeeding before starting ESOBRINT 40 TABLET. It is important to avoid alcohol and certain foods that may worsen acidity, and to be cautious about potential interactions with other medications such as blood thinners, antifungals, and anti-HIV drugs. Prolonged use may lead to deficiencies in vitamin B12, calcium, or magnesium, and may increase the risk of bone thinning (osteoporosis). If you experience symptoms like severe stomach pain, black stools, or allergic reactions, immediate medical attention is necessary. 

During pregnancy and breastfeeding, ESOBRINT 40 TABLET may be used if clearly needed and prescribed by a doctor, as current evidence suggests safety but emphasizes the importance of medical guidance. Common side effects include headache, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, dizziness, and flatulence. Most side effects are mild and temporary, but any persistent or severe symptoms should be reported to your healthcare provider.

mechanismOfAction:
How ESOBRINT 40 TABLET Works
How Does ESOBRINT 40 TABLET Reduce Stomach Acid

ESOBRINT 40 TABLET contains esomeprazole, a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that effectively lowers stomach acid production. It works by blocking the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, located in the stomach lining. This enzyme is responsible for the final step in the secretion of gastric acid. By inhibiting this pump, ESOBRINT 40 TABLET significantly reduces both basal and stimulated acid secretion, providing long-lasting acid suppression and promoting the healing of acid-related conditions

ESOBRINT 40 TABLET action in acid reflux

In acid reflux, stomach acid flows back into the esophagus, causing symptoms like heartburn and discomfort. ESOBRINT 40 TABLET helps manage these symptoms by decreasing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. This reduction in acid not only relieves the burning sensation but also helps protect the esophageal lining from further irritation and damage. The tablet is usually taken before meals for optimal effectiveness, as recommended by healthcare professionals

ESOBRINT 40 TABLET mode of action in peptic ulcer

Peptic ulcers develop when the stomach lining is damaged by excess acid. ESOBRINT 40 TABLET aids in the healing process by suppressing gastric acid secretion through inhibition of the proton pump. With lower acid levels, the ulcerated tissue is given a better environment to recover, reducing pain and the risk of complications. Regular use as directed by a healthcare provider supports ulcer healing and helps prevent recurrence

Is ESOBRINT 40 TABLET More Effective Than H2 Blockers for GERD?

ESOBRINT 40 TABLET (esomeprazole) is generally considered more effective than H2 blockers (H2-receptor antagonists) for treating GERD. Proton pump inhibitors like ESOBRINT 40 TABLET suppress stomach acid more profoundly and for a longer duration than H2 blockers. Clinical studies show that PPIs provide symptomatic relief in about 83% of GERD patients, compared to 60% with H2 blockers. Additionally, healing rates for esophagitis are significantly higher with PPIs—about 78% versus 50% with H2 blockers. This greater efficacy is because PPIs block the final step of acid production, while H2 blockers only partially reduce acid and are less effective, especially after meals. For most patients with moderate to severe GERD, ESOBRINT 40 TABLET is preferred for both symptom control and healing of the esophagus.

Is ESOMEFA 40 TABLET More Effective Than H2 Blockers for GERD?

ESOMEFA 40 TABLET (esomeprazole) is generally considered more effective than H2 blockers (H2-receptor antagonists) for treating GERD. Proton pump inhibitors like ESOMEFA 40 TABLET suppress stomach acid more profoundly and for a longer duration than H2 blockers. Clinical studies show that PPIs provide symptomatic relief in about 83% of GERD patients, compared to 60% with H2 blockers. Additionally, healing rates for esophagitis are significantly higher with PPIs—about 78% versus 50% with H2 blockers. This greater efficacy is because PPIs block the final step of acid production, while H2 blockers only partially reduce acid and are less effective, especially after meals. For most patients with moderate to severe GERD, ESOMEFA 40 TABLET is preferred for both symptom control and healing of the esophagus.

introduction:
Introduction About ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE

ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE is a dual-action formulation designed to support stomach comfort and digestive balance. It contains Rabeprazole and Domperidone, two clinically studied components that reduce excessive stomach acid and support smoother digestion. This combination is widely recommended for individuals experiencing symptoms linked to acidity, heartburn, or discomfort after meals.

Along management with ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE , try to eat less spicy foods and drink plenty of water. Avoid smoking or alcohol consumption as it may aggravate your existing condition. Patients receiving long-term management with the medicine should be kept on regular surveillance to rule out the risk of hypomagnesaemia (decreased magnesium levels in blood) and bone fracture, predominantly in the elderly patients and in patients with other recognized risk factors.

Some individuals may experience mild effects such as headache, dry mouth, abdominal discomfort, constipation, dizziness, or nausea. These effects are generally temporary. If they persist, contact your healthcare provider for guidance.

Store ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight and moisture. Keep out of reach of children and pets.

mechanismOfAction:
How ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE Works

ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE works through a dual mechanism. Rabeprazole acts by reducing acid secretion at its source, ensuring a well-balanced gastric environment. Meanwhile, Domperidone restores the normal movement of the stomach and intestines, managing acid backflow and improving food passage for a more comfortable digestive experience.

Dual Mechanism Explained: Acid Control and Gut Movement

1. Acid Control through Rabeprazole:

Rabeprazole belongs to the class of proton pump modulators that reduce acid secretion at its source. Once absorbed in the intestine, it reaches the acid-producing parietal cells in the stomach lining. Here, it selectively and irreversibly binds to the H/K ATPase enzyme system, also known as the proton pump, the final step in acid secretion. By blocking the hydrogen ion exchange process, Rabeprazole manages excessive acid release into the stomach lumen, thereby increasing gastric pH. It acts faster than many other molecules in its class due to its ability to activate at higher pH levels, efficiently reducing acid production even at minimal acidity. This long-acting acid suppression helps relieve common signs of acidity and promotes a stable digestive environment.

2. Gut Movement through Domperidone:

Domperidone supports the mechanical side of digestion by enhancing gastric motility. It selectively blocks dopamine D2 receptors found in the upper gastrointestinal tract, which normally act to slow stomach contractions. By inhibiting these receptors, Domperidone increases the tone of the lower esophageal sphincter (LES), facilitates faster gastric emptying, and decreases the backward flow of food and acid into the esophagus. It also improves intestinal motion, reducing sensations of bloating, heaviness, or delayed digestion after meals, particularly useful for individuals who experience reflux linked to slow gastric transit.

3. Integrated Digestive Action:

Together, these two mechanisms form a dual-action system. Rabeprazole ensures acid stability, while Domperidone optimizes movement and clearance. This combination supports digestive comfort by minimizing acid build-up while promoting efficient passage of food through the stomach and intestines. It is particularly suited for individuals who face recurring symptoms like heartburn, acid reflux, or post-meal fullness due to poor gastric motility or high acid output. This science-backed synergy makes ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE effective for holistic digestive maintenance under medical supervision.

“Quick Fact Highlights” explaining why the dual combination is clinically valued
Clinically synergistic formulation: The combination of Rabeprazole (20 mg) and Domperidone (30 mg SR) works through a dual mechanism, controlling stomach acid while improving gut motility providing faster and more comprehensive relief from acid discomfort
Science-backed acid regulation: Rabeprazole acts at the final step of acid production by blocking the H/K ATPase enzyme, also known as the proton pump. This action significantly reduces acid secretion and maintains optimal pH levels in the stomach for prolonged comfort
Enhanced digestion support: Domperidone increases the movement of the stomach and upper intestinal tract, promoting quicker stomach emptying and minimizing post-meal bloating, nausea, and reflux symptoms
Faster symptom control: Rabeprazole has one of the quickest onset times among proton pump inhibitors, beginning to act within 1 hour of ingestion, offering prompt relief in cases of severe acidity and heartburn
Persistent gastric balance: The sustained-release form of Domperidone maintains smooth motility throughout the day, managing the recurrence of reflux episodes and late-night acidity, a key benefit for individuals with night-time acid reflux or delayed digestion
Improved patient quality of life: This dual approach relieves not just acid discomfort but also digestive sluggishness, making it beneficial for individuals who experience post-meal heaviness, belching, or regurgitation along with acidity
Clinically preferred for complex acid disorders: Physicians often recommend this combination when single-drug therapy (acid suppressants alone) fails to improve acid-related conditions or reflux-associated nausea
Well-tolerated and safety-monitored: The formulation has a proven safety profile when used as prescribed, with side effects such as mild headache or dizziness typically resolving with continued use

How to use ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE

Take the capsule before meals, preferably in the morning, or as directed by your healthcare provider. Swallow the capsule whole with water without crushing or chewing. Regular use under professional guidance ensures optimal results.

1. How to Take ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE Safely

Swallow the capsule whole with water without biting, breaking, or crushing it. The capsule should not be chewed as it is designed for delayed release. It is best taken on an empty stomach for optimal absorption and faster onset of effect. Avoid taking it with caffeinated or acidic drinks.

2. Dosage and Duration

The dosage and duration depend on your medical condition, age, and response to therapy. Most individuals experience benefits with once-daily use, but in some cases, the doctor may recommend twice-daily administration. Continue the capsule for the prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve early.

3. Dosage Guidelines for Adults and Elderly
For most adult users, the typical dosage is one ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE (Rabeprazole 20 mg + Domperidone 30 mg) taken once daily, ideally 30 minutes before a meal, preferably in the morning. The capsule must be swallowed whole with water, without crushing or chewing, to ensure proper drug release and absorption
Elderly individuals often metabolize medicines more slowly and may have pre-existing heart, kidney, or liver impairments. Therefore, they should only take the prescribed dose once daily, under close medical supervision
Long-term users may require periodic assessment of magnesium, calcium, and vitamin B12 levels, as prolonged use can mildly affect nutrient absorption. Extra caution is advised in those with osteoporosis or history of cardiac arrhythmia, as Domperidone may influence heart rhythm in predisposed individuals

More Information
Why ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE is Doctor-Recommended for “Digestive Balance.”

Digestive discomfort caused by acidity and reflux is often linked to two simultaneous problems excess acid formation and slowed stomach movement.ROLMIZAC D CAPSULE addresses both through a clinically trusted dual mechanism combining Rabeprazole and Domperidone. Doctors recommend this capsule because it supports digestive balance by managing acid levels and enhancing gastric motility, offering smoother stomach function throughout the day.

“Did You Know?” Sidebar: Use small fact highlights like: “Over 70% of acidity cases are linked to late-night meals. Following early dinner routines may reduce reflux frequency”
Over 70% of acidity cases are linked to nighttime eating habits, eating late dinners or snacks within two hours of bedtime significantly increases reflux risk. Having meals earlier in the evening can reduce acid backflow and discomfort.
Meal timing matters: Studies show that eating dinner 3–4 hours before sleep supports better digestion and reduces nighttime acid episodes. Early dining allows the stomach to empty properly before lying down.
Late-night meals affect sleep and metabolism: Research indicates that those who regularly eat after 9 p.m. experience disrupted sleep patterns, slower calorie burning, and more frequent heartburn sensations compared to early eaters.
Fast eating can upset digestive balance: People who eat quickly swallow more air, which increases pressure in the stomach and raises the chance of acid discomfort. Chewing food slowly and mindfully can reduce symptoms and aid smoother digestion.
Simple posture shifts help: Standing or staying upright after meals even for 15–20 minutes can minimize reflux frequency and relieve heaviness. Avoid lying flat immediately after eating.
Diet quality counts: Frequent consumption of spicy, oily, or fried foods can raise stomach acid levels. Choosing gentle foods like oatmeal, bananas, and green vegetables can maintain a neutral digestive pH.
Hydration supports healthy acid balance: Drinking plain water throughout the day dilutes acid concentration naturally. However, sipping slowly instead of gulping helps avoid trapped air and bloating.

introduction:
Introduction About OMIGIFT 20 TABLET

OMIGIFT 20 TABLET contains Omeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called  Proton pump inhibitors. It is used in the management of gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (acid contents in the stomach flow back into the tube connecting your mouth and stomach causing heartburn, nausea, vomiting, bitter taste and discomfort in the upper abdomen) in children (above 1 year of age) and adults.

It is used in adults to manage gastric (stomach), duodenal ulcers (upper part of the intestine), ulcers infected with Helicobacter pylori bacteria in addition to antibiotics (including children) and ulcers due to the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).

Also, it is used in adults to manage Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (increased acid secretion in the stomach due to growth in the pancreas resulting in abdominal pain, diarrhoea, gnawing or discomfort in the upper abdomen, heartburn, nausea and vomiting).

OMIGIFT 20 TABLET is not recommended for use in patients with history of allergic reactions to omeprazole or any other proton pump inhibitors (Ex. pantoprazole, lansoprazole, rabeprazole and esomeprazole).

Before taking OMIGIFT 20 TABLET, tell your doctor if you have any severe liver problems, weight loss, swallowing problems, stomach pain or indigestion, osteoporosis (a condition in which bones become weak and brittle), vitamin B12 deficiency, schedule for a specific blood test (chromogranin A).

OMIGIFT 20 TABLET can be used in pregnant and breastfeeding women only if advised by the doctor. OMIGIFT 20 TABLET should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged above 65 years) due to the increased risk of fractures.

The most common side effects of taking OMIGIFT 20 TABLET are headache, diarrhoea, stomach pain, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects bother you.

introduction:
Introduction About PAN 40MG INJECTION

PAN 40MG INJECTION contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking PAN 40MG INJECTION as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking PAN 40MG INJECTION, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How PAN 40MG INJECTION Works

PAN 40MG INJECTION contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why PAN 40MG INJECTION Is Effective for Acid Control:
PAN 40MG INJECTION effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take PAN 40MG INJECTION?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

introduction:
Introduction About EC PAN 40MG TABLET

EC PAN 40MG TABLET contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking EC PAN 40MG TABLET as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking EC PAN 40MG TABLET, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How EC PAN 40MG TABLET Works

EC PAN 40MG TABLET contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why EC PAN 40MG TABLET Is Effective for Acid Control:
EC PAN 40MG TABLET effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take EC PAN 40MG TABLET?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

More Information
01.What makes EC PAN 40MG TABLET a preferred choice over other medications?
Potent and Long-Lasting Acid Suppression: EC PAN 40MG TABLET contains pantoprazole, a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that effectively blocks the final step of stomach acid production, providing stronger and longer-lasting relief from symptoms like heartburn, acid reflux, and indigestion compared to H2 blockers or antacids.
Comprehensive Symptom Relief and Healing: It not only relieves discomfort from acid-related conditions but also promotes healing of stomach and duodenal ulcers, and helps manage more severe conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
Lowering with Painkiller Use: EC PAN 40MG TABLET is recommended for lowering stomach ulcers and acidity in patients who require long-term use of painkillers (NSAIDs), a benefit not offered by all acid-reducing medicines.
Convenient Once-Daily Dosing: Its long duration of action allows for once-daily dosing, making it easier for patients to adhere to treatment and maintain consistent acid control.
Favorable Tolerability Profile: Most side effects are mild and temporary, such as headache, nausea, or diarrhea. Serious side effects are rare when used as directed, and the risk of complications can be minimized with appropriate monitoring.
Well-Studied and Trusted: Pantoprazole, the active ingredient, is widely used and supported by extensive clinical experience, ensuring both efficacy and safety for a broad range of patients.

These advantages make EC PAN 40MG TABLET a reliable and effective option for both short-term relief and long-term management of acid-related disorders, often outperforming less potent or shorter-acting alternatives.

introduction:
Introduction About ANCOOL SF SUSPENSION

ANCOOL SF SUSPENSION contains Sucralfate, which belongs to the group of medicines called Anti-ulcer agents. It is used for the short-term (up to 8 weeks) management of active duodenal ulcers (part of the small intestine), prophylaxis of gastrointestinal haemorrhage due to stress ulceration in critically ill patients, gastric and benign ulcers.

ANCOOL SF SUSPENSION should be used with caution in patients with chronic renal failure, dialysis patients and diabetes. ANCOOL SF SUSPENSION should be used with caution in pregnant and breastfeeding women. The safety and effectiveness of ANCOOL SF SUSPENSION for use in children have not been established.

ANCOOL SF SUSPENSION should be used with caution in elderly patients above 65 years of age. The most common side effect of taking ANCOOL SF SUSPENSION is constipation. Consult your doctor if any of your symptoms get worse or persist.

introduction:
Introduction About RABLET L CAPSULE

RABLET L CAPSULE is a combination of Levosulpiride and Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Dopamine D2 antagonists and Proton-pump inhibitors respectively. RABLET L CAPSULE is indicated for the management of Gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD). GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the esophagus leading to irritation and inflammation of lining of food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

RABLET L CAPSULE can also be used to manage peptic ulcer (painful sores in the gut), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid), functional dyspepsia (recurrent signs and symptoms of indigestion without an obvious cause) and diabetic gastroparesis (delayed gastric emptying caused due to diabetes).

Take RABLET L CAPSULE preferably on an empty stomach. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking RABLET L CAPSULE as it could potentiate the CNS depressive side effects.

Patients receiving long-term management (>1 year) with RABLET L CAPSULE should be kept on regular surveillance because it can increase the risk of bone fracture (i.e., in the hip, wrist or spine) which is more predominant in the patients having osteoporosis or taking corticosteroids.

Before taking RABLET L CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you have any heart, kidney or liver disease as a precaution. RABLET L CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant or breastfeeding women, including children and adolescents (aged below 18 years).

The most common side effects of taking RABLET L CAPSULE are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation and headache. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsen.

mechanismOfAction:
How RABLET L CAPSULE Works

RABLET L CAPSULE reduces stomach ulcers, nausea and acid reflux, where rabeprazole acts by inhibiting the secretions of stomach acid by blocking the proton pump (H+ K+ ATPase) at the secretory surface of gastric parietal cells and levosulpiride acts by blocking the dopamine D2 receptors in the CTZ (area in medulla oblongata that causes vomiting when stimulated) and in the gut, thus facilitating the movement of food from the stomach into the intestines followed by healing of ulcers or inflammatory lesions in the stomach and in the esophagus.
usageDetails:
How to use RABLET L CAPSULE

Take RABLET L CAPSULE on an empty stomach or as advised by your physician. Swallow RABLET L CAPSULE as a whole and do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

RABLET L CAPSULE should be taken with caution in patients with a previous history of liver problems. Consult your doctor before taking RABLET L CAPSULE.
Do not take RABLET L CAPSULE if you are allergic to Levosulpiride, Rabeprazole or other proton-pump inhibitors (Ex. pantoprazole, omeprazole, lansoprazole).
RABLET L CAPSULE should be taken with caution in patients with asthma or other respiratory diseases. Consult your doctor before taking RABLET L CAPSULE.
RABLET L CAPSULE should be taken with caution in patients with heart disease. Consult your doctor before taking RABLET L CAPSULE.

Others

RABLET L CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you have:

Parkinson’s disease
History of epilepsy
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (a CNS disorder characterized by high fever, stiffness of the muscles, altered mental status (paranoid behavior) and autonomic dysfunction)
Breast cancer (with high levels of prolactin in the body)

Before taking RABLET L CAPSULE, inform your physician if you: 

Have a tumor in the stomach or breast
Have bleeding or perforation of the gastrointestinal tract
Have or at risk of developing vitamin-B12 deficiency
Had developed any skin reaction following management with similar medicines that can reduce stomach acid
Are due to have a specific blood test (Chromogranin A)
Have osteoporosis
Are a smoker
Have porphyria (a rare blood disorder)
Have alcohol intoxication (drinking large amount of alcohol in short period)
Have or had phaeochromocytoma (tumors of adrenal gland) in the past
Have or had prolactinoma (a noncancerous tumor of pituitary gland) in the past
Have hypokalemia (decreased potassium levels in blood)
Have neuroendocrine tumor (tumors in neuroendocrine cells)
Have mania or other mental disorders
Have painful breasts

Use in pediatrics:

RABLET L CAPSULE is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years). Consult your doctor before taking RABLET L CAPSULE.

Use in geriatrics:

RABLET L CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years or above). Consult your doctor before taking RABLET L CAPSULE. Proper dose adjustments and careful monitoring are required in such patients.

Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking RABLET L CAPSULE inform to your doctor, if you are taking any of these medicines:

Medicines used to manage HIV infection (Ex. atazanavir, nelfinavir, saquinavir, rilpivirine)
Antacids (used to neutralize stomach acid secretions) Ex. aluminium hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide
Sucralfate (used to manage duodenal ulcer)
Cisapride (used to manage heart burn in patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease)
Anticholinergics (medicines that causes smooth muscle relaxation and decreases body secretions) Ex. atropine, scopolamine, homatropine
Levodopa (used for parkinson’s disease)
Medicines causing low levels of potassium in blood such as furosemide (used to manage edema), corticosteroids (used to manage inflammation) Ex. cortisol, laxatives such as bisacodyl (used to manage constipation)
Iron salts (used to manage iron deficiency) Ex. ferrous sulphate, ferric ammonium citrate
Medicines used to manage high blood pressure and other heart problems (Ex. captopril, enalapril, losartan, valsartan, diltiazem, digoxin, quinidine)
Atomoxetine (used to manage attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder)
Terfenadine (used to manage allergic conditions)
Chloroquine (used to manage or manage malaria)
Clarithromycin or amoxicillin (used to manage bacterial infections)
Medicines used to manage cancer (Ex. erlotinib, dasatinib, nilotinib)
Methotrexate (used to manage cancer and auto-immune disease)
Tacrolimus or mycophenolate mofetil (used to manage organ rejection after transplant)
Ketoconazole, itraconazole (used to manage fungal infection)
Warfarin (used for blood thinning and management of heart problems)
Pregabalin (used to manage neuropathic pain)
Tramadol (used to manage pain)
Ipratropium (used to manage symptoms of COPD/asthma)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally take too much of RABLET L CAPSULE, contact your doctor immediately or go to a hospital straight away.

introduction:
Introduction About OMIPEP RD TABLET

OMIPEP RD TABLET is a combination of Domperidone and Omeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Prokinetic Drugs and Proton pump inhibitors respectively. It is used to manage peptic ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumours in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid).

OMIPEP RD TABLET is effective in managing peptic ulcer caused either due to stomach infection (H. pylori infection) or due to prolong use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (such as ibuprofen, aceclofenac). OMIPEP RD TABLETacts by reducing the production of gastric acid. It also speeds up the movement of food from the stomach to the intestines, thereby reducing the signs of nausea, vomiting and acid reflux. Due to these actions, it can also reduce the unpleasant signs of GI tract such as nausea, vomiting, indigestion, burping, bloating, acidity or heartburn. OMIPEP RD TABLETis suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 12 years or above weighing 35 kg or more). It should be taken at least 15-30 minutes before meals. During management with OMIPEP RD TABLETyour doctor will closely monitor your kidney functions, liver functions and blood magnesium levels to avoid the risk of unwanted side effects.

Before taking OMIPEP RD TABLETinform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney or heart problems. You must also inform your doctor if you have any blockage or tears in the gut or have weak bones. OMIPEP RD TABLETis not recommended for use in patients having bleeding from the gut. Consult your doctor before taking OMIPEP RD TABLETif you are pregnant or breastfeeding. The most common side effects of taking OMIPEP RD TABLETare dryness of mouth, constipation and flatulence. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect bothers you. You must also inform your doctor immediately if you experience any abnormal signs such as unusual tiredness, abnormal muscle movements, dizziness, confusion, disorientation, irregular heartbeat, fragile bones, bloody stools or vomits or sudden weight loss.

mechanismOfAction:
How OMIPEP RD TABLET Works

OMIPEP RD TABLET contains two medicines namely domperidone and omeprazole. Domperidone works by blocking the actions of a chemical messenger called dopamine in the gut and across the brain and spinal cord. This action stimulates the gut, reduces acid reflux and speeds up the movements of food from the stomach into the intestines. It also blocks the transmission of nerve signals between the vomiting centres and the brain which reduces the onset of nausea and vomiting. Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor. It reduces gastric acid secretion by the blocking the actions of a protein membrane called H+K+Atpase (proton pump) present in the lining of the stomach. By reducing stomach acid production, OMIPEP RD TABLETmanages the worsening of ulcers, heals the existing ulcers and esophageal lesions and provides relief from the unpleasant symptoms of GI tract (such as acidity, bloating, burping and indigestion).

How to use OMIPEP RD TABLET

Take OMIPEP RD TABLET15-30 minutes before meals or as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition. Do not stop taking OMIPEP RD TABLETunless your doctor advice you to stop.

OMIPEP RD TABLET may pass through breast milk. Therefore, it should be used in breastfeeding women only if it is considered necessary by the physician. Consult your doctor for advice.

Driving and Using Machines
USE WITH CAUTION

OMIPEP RD TABLET does not affect your ability in driving or handling heavy tools or machines. However, do not drive or handle heavy tools or machines if your ability is affected by OMIPEP RD TABLET.

Alcohol
CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR

Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking OMIPEP RD TABLET, as it could aggravate your existing condition.

Kidney
USE WITH CAUTION

OMIPEP RD TABLET should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.

Liver
CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR

OMIPEP RD TABLET is not recommended for use in patients with moderate or severe liver impairment. It should be used with caution in patients with other mild liver problems. Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.

Allergy
CONTRAINDICATED

Do not take OMIPEP RD TABLETif you are allergic to Domperidone, Omeprazole or to any other proton pump inhibitors (such as rabeprazole, pantoprazole).

Heart Disease
CONTRAINDICATED

OMIPEP RD TABLET is not recommended for use in patients with heart problems such as prolongation of QT interval or congestive heart failure. Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.

Use In Pediatrics
CONTRAINDICATED

OMIPEP RD TABLET should be used in children and adolescents (aged 12 years or above, weighing 35kg or more). It is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 12 years). However, consult your doctor before taking it.

Use In Geriatrics
USE WITH CAUTION

OMIPEP RD TABLET should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years and above). Therefore, consult your doctor before taking it.

name: VISCO Liquid 200ml
introduction:
Introduction About VISCO LIQUID

Visco Syrup is an Antacid, Anti-Reflux and Anti-flatulent used to relieve reflex esophagitis, heart burn and reflux associated with Gastro Oesophageal Reflux Disorder. It contains Sodium Alginate, Magnesium Hydroxide, Aluminium Hydroxide, and Simethicone as active ingredients.

Magnesium Hydroxide and Aluminium hydroxide are antacids works by neutralising acid in the stomach. Simethicone is an anti-gas agent works by breaking down gas bubbles in the stomach and intestine, thereby allowing the exit of the gas. Sodium alginate forms a gel like barrier over the stomach and manages the reflux of acid back into the food pipe.

Always use Visco Syrup as advised by your doctor. It is for external use only. Shake well before use. Take 1 to 2 teaspoonful 3 to 4 times a day after meals or as directed by the physician.

name: Rabifast XL Capsule 10'S
introduction:
Introduction About RABIFAST XL CAPSULE

RABIFAST XL CAPSULE is a combination of Levosulpiride and Rabeprazole which belongs to the group of medicines called Dopamine D2 antagonists and Proton-pump inhibitors respectively. RABIFAST XL CAPSULE is indicated for the management of Gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD). GERD is a chronic digestive disease in which the stomach acid frequently flows into the esophagus leading to irritation and inflammation of lining of food pipe. Symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, nausea, sensation of lump in throat and stomach discomfort.

RABIFAST XL CAPSULE can also be used to manage peptic ulcer (painful sores in the gut), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in pancreas causing the stomach to secrete more acid), functional dyspepsia (recurrent signs and symptoms of indigestion without an obvious cause) and diabetic gastroparesis (delayed gastric emptying caused due to diabetes).

Take RABIFAST XL CAPSULE preferably on an empty stomach. Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE as it could potentiate the CNS depressive side effects.

Patients receiving long-term management (>1 year) with RABIFAST XL CAPSULE should be kept on regular surveillance because it can increase the risk of bone fracture (i.e., in the hip, wrist or spine) which is more predominant in the patients having osteoporosis or taking corticosteroids.

Before taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you have any heart, kidney or liver disease as a precaution. RABIFAST XL CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant or breastfeeding women, including children and adolescents (aged below 18 years).

The most common side effects of taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE are nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation and headache. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsen.
usesDetails:
Uses Of RABIFAST XL CAPSULE
Manage Gastro-Esophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)

Manage peptic ulcer
Manage Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
Manage diabetic gastroparesis
mechanismOfAction:
How RABIFAST XL CAPSULE Works

RABIFAST XL CAPSULE reduces stomach ulcers, nausea and acid reflux, where rabeprazole acts by inhibiting the secretions of stomach acid by blocking the proton pump (H+ K+ ATPase) at the secretory surface of gastric parietal cells and levosulpiride acts by blocking the dopamine D2 receptors in the CTZ (area in medulla oblongata that causes vomiting when stimulated) and in the gut, thus facilitating the movement of food from the stomach into the intestines followed by healing of ulcers or inflammatory lesions in the stomach and in the esophagus.
usageDetails:
How to use RABIFAST XL CAPSULE

Take RABIFAST XL CAPSULE on an empty stomach or as advised by your physician. Swallow RABIFAST XL CAPSULE as a whole and do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

RABIFAST XL CAPSULE is strictly not recommended for use in breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE.
Do not drive or operate any heavy tools or machines if you experience dizziness, drowsiness or sleepiness after taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE.

Avoid consumption of alcohol while taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE, as it could cause CNS depression (characterized by confusion, attention impairment and anxiety), dizziness and/or drowsiness. Consult your doctor before taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE.
RABIFAST XL CAPSULE should be taken with caution in patients with kidney disease. Consult your doctor before taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE.
RABIFAST XL CAPSULE should be taken with caution in patients with a previous history of liver problems. Consult your doctor before taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE.
Do not take RABIFAST XL CAPSULE if you are allergic to Levosulpiride, Rabeprazole or other proton-pump inhibitors (Ex. pantoprazole, omeprazole, lansoprazole).
RABIFAST XL CAPSULE should be taken with caution in patients with asthma or other respiratory diseases. Consult your doctor before taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE.
RABIFAST XL CAPSULE should be taken with caution in patients with heart disease. Consult your doctor before taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE.

Others

RABIFAST XL CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you have:

Parkinson’s disease
History of epilepsy
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (a CNS disorder characterized by high fever, stiffness of the muscles, altered mental status (paranoid behavior) and autonomic dysfunction)
Breast cancer (with high levels of prolactin in the body)

Before taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE, inform your physician if you: 

Have a tumor in the stomach or breast
Have bleeding or perforation of the gastrointestinal tract
Have or at risk of developing vitamin-B12 deficiency
Had developed any skin reaction following management with similar medicines that can reduce stomach acid
Are due to have a specific blood test (Chromogranin A)
Have osteoporosis
Are a smoker
Have porphyria (a rare blood disorder)
Have alcohol intoxication (drinking large amount of alcohol in short period)
Have or had phaeochromocytoma (tumors of adrenal gland) in the past
Have or had prolactinoma (a noncancerous tumor of pituitary gland) in the past
Have hypokalemia (decreased potassium levels in blood)
Have neuroendocrine tumor (tumors in neuroendocrine cells)
Have mania or other mental disorders
Have painful breasts

Use in pediatrics:

RABIFAST XL CAPSULE is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years). Consult your doctor before taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE.

Use in geriatrics:

RABIFAST XL CAPSULE should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years or above). Consult your doctor before taking RABIFAST XL CAPSULE. Proper dose adjustments and careful monitoring are required in such patients.

introduction:
Introduction About PANTOCID 40MG INJECTION

PANTOCID 40MG INJECTION contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking PANTOCID 40MG INJECTION as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking PANTOCID 40MG INJECTION, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How PANTOCID 40MG INJECTION Works

PANTOCID 40MG INJECTION contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why PANTOCID 40MG INJECTION Is Effective for Acid Control:
PANTOCID 40MG INJECTION effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take PANTOCID 40MG INJECTION?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

Potent and Long-Lasting Acid Suppression: PANTOCID 40MG INJECTION contains pantoprazole, a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that effectively blocks the final step of stomach acid production, providing stronger and longer-lasting relief from symptoms like heartburn, acid reflux, and indigestion compared to H2 blockers or antacids.

introduction:
Introduction About S PPI 40 TABLET

S PPI 40 TABLET, containing esomeprazole, is widely chosen by individuals seeking relief from persistent acidity, heartburn, and acid reflux symptoms. It is especially useful for those experiencing discomfort due to gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcers, erosive esophagitis, or conditions involving excessive stomach acid production such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. By blocking the proton pumps in the stomach lining, esomeprazole effectively reduces acid secretion, promoting healing of the stomach and esophageal lining and improving overall digestive comfort. 

This tablet is ideal for adults and can also be considered for use in elderly patients, pregnant or breastfeeding women, and those with kidney or liver conditions, though it should only be used under medical supervision in these groups. S PPI 40 TABLET is generally taken once daily, preferably before meals, and should be swallowed whole with water—crushing or chewing the tablet is not recommended for optimal absorption. Consistency in timing and adherence to the prescribed duration are important for achieving the best results. 

Patients are advised to inform their healthcare provider about any existing allergies, liver problems, or plans for pregnancy or breastfeeding before starting S PPI 40 TABLET. It is important to avoid alcohol and certain foods that may worsen acidity, and to be cautious about potential interactions with other medications such as blood thinners, antifungals, and anti-HIV drugs. Prolonged use may lead to deficiencies in vitamin B12, calcium, or magnesium, and may increase the risk of bone thinning (osteoporosis). If you experience symptoms like severe stomach pain, black stools, or allergic reactions, immediate medical attention is necessary. 

During pregnancy and breastfeeding, S PPI 40 TABLET may be used if clearly needed and prescribed by a doctor, as current evidence suggests safety but emphasizes the importance of medical guidance. Common side effects include headache, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, dizziness, and flatulence. Most side effects are mild and temporary, but any persistent or severe symptoms should be reported to your healthcare provider.

How Does S PPI 40 TABLET Reduce Stomach Acid

S PPI 40 TABLET contains esomeprazole, a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that effectively lowers stomach acid production. S PPI 40 TABLET action in acid reflux

In acid reflux, stomach acid flows back into the esophagus, causing symptoms like heartburn and discomfort. S PPI 40 TABLET helps manage these symptoms by decreasing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. This reduction in acid not only relieves the burning sensation but also helps protect the esophageal lining from further irritation and damage. The tablet is usually taken before meals for optimal effectiveness, as recommended by healthcare professionals

S PPI 40 TABLET mode of action in peptic ulcer

Peptic ulcers develop when the stomach lining is damaged by excess acid. S PPI 40 TABLET aids in the healing process by suppressing gastric acid secretion through inhibition of the proton pump. With lower acid levels, the ulcerated tissue is given a better environment to recover, reducing pain and the risk of complications. Regular use as directed by a healthcare provider supports ulcer healing and helps prevent recurrence

Is S PPI 40 TABLET More Effective Than H2 Blockers for GERD?

S PPI 40 TABLET (esomeprazole) is generally considered more effective than H2 blockers (H2-receptor antagonists) for treating GERD. Proton pump inhibitors like S PPI 40 TABLET suppress stomach acid more profoundly and for a longer duration than H2 blockers. Clinical studies show that PPIs provide symptomatic relief in about 83% of GERD patients, compared to 60% with H2 blockers. Additionally, healing rates for esophagitis are significantly higher with PPIs—about 78% versus 50% with H2 blockers. This greater efficacy is because PPIs block the final step of acid production, while H2 blockers only partially reduce acid and are less effective, especially after meals. For most patients with moderate to severe GERD, S PPI 40 TABLET is preferred for both symptom control and healing of the esophagus.

Introduction About LENOCARB M PLUS ORAL SUSPENSION

LENOCARB M PLUS ORAL SUSPENSION is a combination of Magaldrate, Oxetacaine, and Simethicone, which belongs to the group of medicines called Antacid, Local Anaesthetic and Anti-flatulence, respectively. It is used for the management of acidity, heartburn, gas, and stomach ulcers. The stomach is generally protected from acid by a mucous layer.

In some cases, due to excess production of acid, the mucous layer gets eroded, which leads to problems like acidity and heartburn. Bloating occurs when the abdomen is filled with air or gas. Avoid smoking and alcohol consumption while taking LENOCARB M PLUS ORAL SUSPENSION, as it leads to increased production of stomach acid, thereby increasing acidity and heartburn.

LENOCARB M PLUS ORAL SUSPENSION is not recommended for use in patients with hepatic and renal impairments. LENOCARB M PLUS ORAL SUSPENSION is not recommended for use by pregnant or breastfeeding women. LENOCARB M PLUS ORAL SUSPENSION is not recommended for use in children, and it should be used with caution in elderly patients. The most common side effects of taking LENOCARB M PLUS ORAL SUSPENSION are nausea, vomiting, constipation, diarrhea, and dry mouth. Consult your doctor if any of your symptoms get worse or persist.

introduction:
Introduction About PANTIAC 40MG TABLET

PANTIAC 40MG TABLET contains Pantoprazole, which belongs to the group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It is commonly prescribed to manage conditions caused by excess stomach acid such as acidity, heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is also prescribed to control stomach ulcers and acidity that can occur with long-term use of painkillers. Pantoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, thereby providing relief from symptoms associated with these acid-related disorders.

For optimal effect, take this medicine one hour before meals, preferably in the morning. The dosage will be determined by your doctor based on your medical condition and response to management. Continue taking PANTIAC 40MG TABLET as directed, even if your symptoms improve quickly. You can help enhance the effectiveness of your management by eating smaller, more frequent meals and avoiding caffeinated beverages (such as tea and coffee), as well as spicy or fatty foods.  

The most common side effects observed with this medicine include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, flatulence, diarrhea, stomach pain, constipation, and rash. These effects are usually mild, but if they persist or become bothersome, consult your doctor. Prolonged use of this medication may increase the risk of certain side effects, for example, taking it for more than one year, especially at higher doses, may raise your risk of bone fractures. Discuss management measures for bone loss, such as calcium and vitamin D supplementation, with your doctor if you require long-term management.

Before taking PANTIAC 40MG TABLET, inform your doctor if you have severe liver problems, are taking medicines for HIV, have a history of allergic reactions to pantoprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, or suffer from bone loss (osteoporosis). Pregnant or breastfeeding women should also consult their doctor before taking it.

mechanismOfAction:
How PANTIAC 40MG TABLET Works

PANTIAC 40MG TABLET contains pantoprazole, which is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It works by specifically targeting and blocking the proton pumps (H+/K+ ATPase enzymes) located in the stomach lining, which are responsible for the final step in the production of gastric acid.

Pantoprazole Mechanism of Action Explained:
Pantoprazole accumulates in the acidic environment of the stomach’s parietal cells, where it is converted to its active form. This active form binds irreversibly to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also known as the gastric proton pump, on the secretory surface of the parietal cell. By forming covalent bonds with this enzyme, pantoprazole effectively inactivates it, thereby blocking both basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Understanding Proton Pump Inhibition:
Proton pumps are specialized enzymes (H+/K+ ATPase) found in the stomach’s parietal cells. They are responsible for the final step in the secretion of hydrochloric acid (HCl) into the stomach. By inhibiting these pumps, pantoprazole stops the secretion of acid regardless of the original stimulus, leading to a significant and sustained reduction in stomach acidity.

Role of H+/K+ ATPase in Acid Secretion:
The H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, also called the gastric proton pump, exchanges hydrogen ions (protons) from the parietal cell with potassium ions from the stomach lumen. This exchange results in the secretion of hydrochloric acid, which is essential for digestion but can cause problems like ulcers and acid reflux if produced in excess. Pantoprazole’s action on this enzyme interrupts this process, reducing acid output.

Why PANTIAC 40MG TABLET Is Effective for Acid Control:
PANTIAC 40MG TABLET effectiveness stems from its ability to irreversibly inhibit the proton pumps, resulting in a longer-lasting suppression of acid production compared to other classes of acid-reducing drugs. Since new pumps must be synthesized by the body before acid secretion can resume, the acid-suppressing effect persists for over 24 hours, even after the drug has been cleared from the bloodstream.

What Happens in the Stomach When You Take PANTIAC 40MG TABLET?
After ingestion, pantoprazole is absorbed and transported to the parietal cells in the stomach. In the acidic environment of these cells, it is activated and binds to the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme, inactivating it. This leads to a marked reduction in gastric acid secretion, which helps relieve symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn, and promotes the healing of ulcers and esophagitis.

Duration and Effectiveness of Pantoprazole:
Pantoprazole has a relatively long duration of action due to its irreversible binding to the proton pump. Its acid-suppressing effects last for more than 24 hours, even though its plasma half-life is only about two hours. This allows for convenient once-daily dosing, and its efficacy is comparable to other PPIs, making it a reliable option for both short-term and long-term management of acid-related disorders.

Potent and Long-Lasting Acid Suppression: PANTIAC 40MG TABLET contains pantoprazole, a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that effectively blocks the final step of stomach acid production, providing stronger and longer-lasting relief from symptoms like heartburn, acid reflux, and indigestion compared to H2 blockers or antacids.
Comprehensive Symptom Relief and Healing: It not only relieves discomfort from acid-related conditions but also promotes healing of stomach and duodenal ulcers, and helps manage more severe conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
Lowering with Painkiller Use: PANTIAC 40MG TABLET is recommended for lowering stomach ulcers and acidity in patients who require long-term use of painkillers (NSAIDs), a benefit not offered by all acid-reducing medicines.

Well-Studied and Trusted: Pantoprazole, the active ingredient, is widely used and supported by extensive clinical experience, ensuring both efficacy and safety for a broad range of patients.

These advantages make PANTIAC 40MG TABLET a reliable and effective option for both short-term relief and long-term management of acid-related disorders, often outperforming less potent or shorter-acting alternatives.
